Sports.title: ‘This may look a strange decision’ – York City SACK manager Stuart Maynard despite promotion to EFL with 108 points
Sports.content:
YORK CITY have confirmed the exit of manager Stuart Maynard just months after he guided the club back into the English Football League after a decade away.

York won the National League in dramatic circumstances in April, scoring an equaliser in the 103rd minute to draw with title rivals Rochdale – who would have been champions themselves had they won.



But Maynard won’t get to see the fruits of his labour. The club says they had a “difference in direction and vision for the football club,” with Maynard.

A club statement read: “York City Football Club can confirm that Stuart Maynard will be leaving his role as First Team Manager, with immediate effect.



“This has not been an easy decision, and it is not one the board has taken lightly.

“Ultimately, it comes down to a difference in direction and vision for the football club. We recognise that, from the outside, this may look like a strange or difficult decision to understand.



“But we believe that in the long term, the football club will be in a stronger position because of it, another step towards the vision we, as custodians of this club, believe will deliver sustained success.

“Like every one of you, we love this football club, and we would never make a decision we didn’t believe was in its best long-term interests. We hope our track record of improving year on year has earned us a degree of trust, and we understand that not everyone will agree with, or fully understand, this decision right away.

“We would like to thank Stuart for his contribution to York City FC and wish him well for the future.”

The club have not left themselves long to figure things out.

ANDONI IRAOLA’S start to life as Liverpool boss was bittersweet as they beat Sunderland but lost Joe Gomez to injury.

The Reds pre-season kicked off with a clash against familiar Premier League opposition in Sunderland in the USA.



Iraola’s side won 4-2, courtesy of goals from Kieran Morrison, Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas.

However, in a bitter blow Liverpool were forced to take off 29-year-old defender Gomez – who started the game in centre-back and wearing the captain’s armband – just eight minutes in.



Speaking after the game, Iraola said: “Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe.

“We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we’ve lost Joe straight away.”

Former Charlton star Gomez played 33 times under Arne Slot last season, but only started 16 of those games as he battled a number of small knocks including hamstring, knee, muscle and Achilles problems.

Liverpool were without club captain Virgil van Dijk, who is on holiday following this participation at the World Cup with the Netherlands, and new £60million signing Jeremy Jacquet.

Iraola warned earlier this week his squad was “very thin” in defence, a point which sporting director Richard Hughes might have seen hammered home as he watched the game taking place in Nashville.

With Gomez going off injured, it meant 18-year-old’s Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe were left to marshal the defence, and performed admirably considering the circumstances.

Sports.title: Harry Redknapp warns FA to avoid Pep Guardiola and claims ‘sleepwalking’ England face an Italy-style World Cup nightmare
Sports.content:
HARRY REDKNAPP warns English football is sleepwalking into an Italy-style nightmare — and insists the FA must NOT chase Pep Guardiola.

The former West Ham and Tottenham boss says Thomas Tuchel needs total backing while insisting England’s academy system is quietly collapsing.



With Guardiola turning down the Italy job, Redknapp insists Wembley chiefs should steer away from targeting the former Manchester City manager.

Redknapp said: “Everybody seems to think Pep is some sort of magic wand in football. The bloke is an absolute tactical genius, no doubt about it.



“But you can’t just teleport Pep into the England set-up and suddenly expect guaranteed trophies.

“At club level, Pep’s always had massive money to spend. If he needs a full-back who can step into midfield, he buys a £70million player.



“In international football, there are no chequebooks. You don’t have transfer windows. You get what your country produces, and that’s the end of the story.”

And Redknapp has grave concerns about the future production line of English talent and fears not enough are coming through.

He said: “Italy is a proper warning sign for us. A massive footballing powerhouse missing out on back-to-back World Cups is absolute madness — criminal really.

“Yet, if we aren’t careful, we are sleepwalking straight into the exact same disaster.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“The pipeline of young local talent in Italy has dried up and it’s starting to happen here.”

Having overseen one of the most prolific academy eras in modern English football, Redknapp believes top-flight clubs are drastically undermining their own local production lines.

He said: “Back in my day at West Ham, we had a proper production line coming through — Michael Carrick, Joe Cole, Rio Ferdinand, Frank Lampard, Glen Johnson, Jermain Defoe.

“We had players bursting into the team who lived and breathed the club, knew the culture, and went on to play for the Three Lions.



“It breaks my heart because half these academy boys now don’t even get to watch the first team train. They’re stuck on faraway pitch behind high fences.

“At West Ham, we had the lads sweeping the terraces, staying behind after training, kicking balls against walls and watching the senior pros.

“Now everything is sanitised. You can’t build steel in kids if you insulate them from real senior football.”

To fix the crisis, Redknapp called for strict policy changes within the Premier League, urging that clubs be forced to field homegrown players rather than buying foreign squad options.



Redknapp said: “There should be rules in place where Premier League clubs have to field a set number of English players. That’s how you protect our future.

“Right now, top clubs just go abroad to buy ready-made players, and our young homegrown lads get blocked at every turn.”

Maintaining his traditionalist view on international management, Redknapp argued that national teams should strictly employ managers from their own country.

He said: “In an ideal world, an English national team should be led by an English manager.

“The Spain manager is Spanish. The France manager is French. The Argentina manager was Argentinian who used to play for West Ham!



“We’ve got brilliant managers like Eddie Howe who know our culture.

“Plus top former players like Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard who have cut their teeth in management.

“But it’s clear the only way English managers usually get Premier League jobs is if they get promoted from the Championship.



“If we don’t trust and back our own coaches, what message are we sending to the next generation?”

Redknapp urged the nation to get behind the current boss Tuchel for the task ahead while fixing the long-term system.

The former manager said: “Don’t get me wrong, we’ve actually got a fantastic squad of players right now who are more than good enough to go and win a major trophy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“So let’s forget about chasing Pep. Let’s give Tuchel our full backing for the job ahead.

“And let’s sort out our youth development before we end up like the Italians, watching the World Cup from the sofa at home.”

Sports.title: Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star
Sports.content:
With the Premier League on course to smash its spending record, it's worth reminding them that you don't always have to splash out on signings. Sometimes the best transfers cost nothing - well, bar a hefty a signing-on bonus.

From Ruud Gullit to Chelsea and Sol Campbell to Arsenal, to James Milner to Liverpool and Zlatan Ibrahimovic to Manchester United, the Premier League has seen its fair share of excellent free transfers down the years.

So who could be next? There are plenty of stars from around the world who find themselves without a club, some of them more familiar to English sides than others.

As the final month of the summer transfer window nears, let's build an XI of free agents.

‌

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

Goalkeeper: Stefan Ortega

Perhaps the least stacked position in this team, former Manchester City and Nottingham Forest star Stefan Ortega looks the standout goalkeeper available on a free. Ex-Brighton shot-stopper Matthew Ryan is another looking for his next move, while former Aston Villa man Orjan Nyland will hope that his World Cup performances convince someone to come knocking.

Right-back: Dani Carvajal

Arguably the best right-back of his generation, Dani Carvajal left Real Madrid this summer after two spells covering 23 years in which he won 27 major trophies. The Spaniard has reportedly received proposals from the Saudi Pro League, Major League Soccer and Inter Milan, but he remains out of work.

Centre-back: John Stones

John Stones was a somewhat surprise inclusion in the England squad after making just 38 appearances in his final two seasons with Manchester City, but he ended up starting both the quarter-finals and semi-finals in a show of faith from Thomas Tuchel. His experience and quality on the ball makes him an attractive prospect for clubs willing to take a risk on his dubious fitness, with Chelsea and Arsenal linked.

‌



Which club should sign John Stones? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images John Stones was released by Manchester City (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Centre-back: David Alaba

Another departure from Madrid, David Alaba's last three years have been ravaged by injury, missing a total of 126 games for club and country. The ex-Bayern Munich star still managed to be a starter at the World Cup, so that may well convince another European giant to snap him up.

Left-back: Oleksandr Zinchenko

Two clubs, 12 games and one serious injury - that was the story of Oleksandr Zinchenko's season. Following a disappointing loan spell with Nottingham Forest, Arsenal sold him to Ajax for just £1.3million.

‌



But the Ukrainian was only given a short-term deal before suffering a knee injury which is set to rule him out for well into the new season. Zinchenko has proven himself in the Premier League, but will his rehab put clubs off signing him this summer?

View 5 Images Injury ruined Oleksandr Zinchenko's spell with Ajax before it got going (Image: Roy Lazet/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Centre midfield: Franck Kessie

Franck Kessie knows all about getting a big move on a free transfer. The Ivorian moved to Barcelona after his contract with AC Milan expired in 2022, and he memorably scored the goal that won Xavi Hernandez's side the La Liga title in his one and only season.

Kessie was then sold to Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, where he spent the past three seasons. But now he's without a club and tipped for a return to Italy with Juventus.

‌



Centre midfield: Leon Goretzka

After eight years and 15 trophies with Bayern Munich, Leon Goretzka is another free agent with serious pedigree to offer. The German went to the World Cup but has been tipped for an immediate return to the United States, with Chicago Fire heavily linked with what would be their second marquee signing of the summer after acquiring Robert Lewandowski.

View 5 Images Leon Goretzka went to the World Cup with Germany (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

Centre midfield: Julian Brandt

Staying in the Bundesliga and Julian Brandt has left Borussia Dortmund. The versatile playmaker is said to have offers from Leeds and Ajax, while Arsenal, Aston Villa and Barcelona have also been linked.

Midfield is where some real bargains are to be had. Other options include Yves Bissouma, Dani Ceballos, Fabinho and Lorenzo Pellegrini.

‌



Right wing: Mo Salah

No doubt the most high-profile name in this team, Mo Salah still hasn't found a new club three months after his departure from Liverpool was announced. For a player of his stature and still impeccably fit at 34 years old, that's a surprise.

But factor in the World Cup and it's understandable that the Egypt captain has had other priorities. Speculation over his next destination has been building in the past fortnight, though, with Sporting Kansas City lining up an ambition move and cash-rich Saudi clubs also keen.

According to reports, his priority to stay in Europe. Could a Premier League club offer him a deal?

View 5 Images Mo Salah has left Liverpool after nine years (Image: Jack Thomas/Getty Images)

‌



Striker: Dusan Vlahovic

When Juventus paid £66m for Dusan Vlahovic in 2022, few doubted that he'd become one of Europe's most prolific No.9s. But fast forward four years and he's without an employer.

Barcelona continue to be linked with the ex-Fiorentina marksman while there's been speculation that Juventus could resume talks over a new contract, having failed to agree on an extension before the end of the season. Watch this space.

Left wing: Jadon Sancho

Finally, a name more than familiar to English fans. Jadon Sancho's deal with Manchester United ran out last month and Aston Villa, who he spent last season on loan with, don't want to sign him permanently.

A return to former club Borussia Dortmund has long been rumoured, having also had a loan spell there in 2024. Sancho is still just 26 and has plenty of magic to offer if he can find the right landing spot this summer.

Sports.content:
Arsenal learn fee and transfer conditions to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid

Real Madrid are reportedly demanding big-money for Vinicius Jr this summer, with Arsenal exploring a move for the Brazilian winger

View 2 Images Arsenal are interested in signing Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty Images)

Real Madrid are reportedly demanding at least €160million (£137m) for Vinicius Junior amid Arsenal's interest. The Gunners are considering a swoop for the winger, with Real Madrid determined to avoid losing the Brazil international on a free transfer when his contract runs out next summer.

‌



The 26-year-old is viewed as an option to strengthen Arsenal's left flank as they seek to cement their position as Premier League champions under Mikel Arteta. The forward notched 22 goals and registered 14 assists in 53 outings for Los Blancos last season - despite the Spanish giants experiencing a disappointing campaign.

‌



And with negotiations over fresh terms at the Santiago Bernabeu having reportedly hit an impasse, it could present an ideal chance for Arteta's side to secure one of the game's premier attacking talents.

‌



Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

However, Spanish publication SPORT claims that the Gunners will be required to shatter the British transfer record to capture him. Alexander Isak's £125m switch from Newcastle United to Liverpool last summer stands as the current highest sum.

Should Arsenal meet the reported £137m asking price, they would eclipse that record by a minimum of £12m, though Real may demand more. The report in SPORT also indicates that the La Liga club will refuse to enter discussions unless the figure is satisfied.

It's understood that the 15-time Champions League champions wish to establish a sufficiently high threshold to discourage speculative enquiries regarding any transfer, including add-ons tied to performance and silverware secured.

‌



View 2 Images Vinicius Jr only has a year or so left on his contract at Real Madrid (Image: Photo by Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It's reported that the player and club arranged to convene at the conclusion of July to explore a potential contract extension - with Arsenal certain to monitor developments closely should negotiations falter.

‌



Real manager Jose Mourinho has allegedly made his position clear that he desires Vinicius Jr. to stay at the Spanish capital outfit. The Telegraph reports that Mourinho would oppose the notion of the Brazilian departing the Santiago Bernabeu to finalise a switch to Arteta's side.

However, Real may require raising capital, as reports indicate they are contemplating a £102m pursuit of RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande. Arsenal are also understood to have lodged an enquiry for the Ivorian. Yet if Diomande opts for Real, that could heighten the likelihood of Vinicius Jr. arriving at the Emirates Stadium this summer.

‌



Despite astonishment surrounding a potential acquisition of the Los Blancos star, Arteta has demonstrated an ambition for the club to compete for the world's elite talent.

In 2024, when Kylian Mbappe was poised to depart Paris Saint-Germain upon expiry of his contract, Arteta was direct in his answer when questioned whether Arsenal needed to enter the race for such players. "Exactly," he replied.

"Why not? If we want to be the best team, then you need to have the best players, that's for sure."

He added: "When there is a player of that calibre, we always have to be in that conversation. But it looks in a different way, that's what I would say."

Sports.title: Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief
Sports.content:
Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief

Michael Olise's future has been a hot topic throughout the summer transfer window, with Liverpool in the queue of clubs who would like to sign him from Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Michael Olise is a man in demand (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund has told Liverpool to forget about signing Michael Olise, as he 'will' be playing in Germany again next season. Olise, 24, has been strongly linked with a move to Liverpool amid their search for a wide forward to replace Mo Salah.

‌



Real Madrid are also interested in signing the Frenchman, who was superb at the World Cup. Olise provided seven assists in eight games, building on an outstanding season with Bayern.

‌



The winger racked up 48 goals and assists in 52 games as Vincent Kompany's side ran away with the Bundesliga title and won the DfB Pokal. It's no wonder that Bayern want to keep Olise are reportedly preparing to offer him a bumper new contract.

‌



But as for his immediate future, Freund is relaxed. Asked specifically about Real's interest and claims that Olise is desperate to join Los Blancos, the Bayern chief replied: "This is absolutely not an issue for us.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We're delighted that Michael is back from his holiday. He'll play an important role for FC Bayern this season, just as he did last season, too."

‌



Freund was speaking after a youthful Bayern side lost 2-1 against third-tier Wehen Wiesbaden in a friendly. Big-name stars such as Olise and Harry Kane are expected to feature later in pre-season.

Last month, it was reported that Real had submitted a £130million bid for Olise. However, the Spanish giants issued a statement saying that there had been no 'direct or indirect' with the 24-year-old.

Should Michael Olise leave Bayern Munich? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Christoph Freund insists that Michael Olise is going nowhere (Image: S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images)

Part of the statement read: "Real Madrid also wishes to highlight the excellent institutional relationship it maintains with Bayern Munich -- with whom it shares a long history of mutual respect, collaboration, and admiration -- and regrets the circulation of speculation which does not reflect reality."

Given Bayern's firm stance, both Liverpool and Real have been forced to identify alternatives to Olise. One of them is RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, who Real are said to have bid £85m for this week.

Article continues below

Leipzig rejected the offer and are demanding a fee of at least £100m. Liverpool are also looking at Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche to bolster Andoni Iraola's squad.

Sports.title: Real Madrid told to approve Arsenal's Vinicius transfer because 'they cannot rely' on him
Sports.content:
Real Madrid told to approve Arsenal's Vinicius transfer because 'they cannot rely' on him

Arsenal are keen on Vinicius Jnr and Real Madrid have been encouraged to consider a culture reset and cash in on the forward, whose contract is winding down

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr has been linked with a Real Madrid exit

Real Madrid have been told that selling Vinicius Jr can allow them to reset the dressing room with PSG's success showcasing how a team ethic will outdo quality individuals.

‌



The Brazilian has become the subject of one of the summer's biggest transfer stories to date with Arsenal weighing up a move. No bid has yet been tabled, but internally they are keen on the forward, whose contract continues to wind down.

‌



Vinicius has been at Real since 2018 and become a leading light, helping them twice win the Champions League. He's on mammoth wages and is seeking parity with Kylian Mbappe, but negotiations are being done off the back of a second successive trophyless season at the Bernabeu.

‌



Real's fortunes have nosedived and Emmanuel Petit believes ridding of one of their biggest names could allow them to change the culture - citing the success PSG have enjoyed since losing Mbappe and adopting a more collective approach.

Real Madrid president has already made Vinicius Jr to Arsenal stance very clear READ MORE :

He told the Evening Standard: “Something has to be rebuilt in Madrid. It started with the manager in the dressing room, but also with the players on the pitch. You cannot rely all the time on the brilliance of Mbappé or Vinícius, they have to stop that.

“Spain and PSG have sent strong messages over the last two seasons that the team matters. It's not based on the individual, it's about the team's unity. You can have the best players in some positions, but it doesn't mean you're going to win the games and the competition.

‌



“Mourinho wants to get strong and reliable players, and I'm pretty sure he's putting pressure on Florentino to spend the money wisely. I know some big players are targets. If they can do that, it could be a very good season for Mourinho and for Madrid.”

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho has already landed four new faces at Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

The Special One has signed Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva on free transfers whilst also bringing in Marc Cucurella and Denzel Dumfries.

Article continues below

Arsenal are looking to bolster their forward line after narrowly missing out on a Premier League and Champions League double. They were edged out in the European Cup final with their lack of firepower cited as an area where they can improve their squad. They have now discussed addinfg Vinicius, who would be among the most blockbuster signings they've ever made.

Sports.title: Wolves release statement after player involved in viral England under-16 fight video
Sports.content:
Wolves release statement after player involved in viral England under-16 fight video

Footage of two England under-16 players fighting inside a hotel room as their team-mates watched emerged on social media this week, and now Wolves have confirmed that one of their academy prospects was involved

View Image The two England players were filmed fighting

Wolves have issued a statement confirming that a member of their academy was one of the players filmed fighting a team-mate during an England under-16 camp in Turkey last year. Footage emerged on social media this week showing the pair scrapping in a hotel room, as other players watched on.

‌



Several of their team-mates were filming the incident and could be heard encouraging them. The FA issued a statement saying that the fight was caused by an 'internal matter' and was 'quickly resolved'.

‌



Championship club Wolves have now addressed the viral video in a statement published on their website, saying that the footage only captures part of a 'broader sequence of events'. It read: "Wolves are aware of footage from a previous England youth camp involving one the club's academy players which has recently resurfaced on social media.

‌



"The club is satisfied that the widely shared footage captures only part of a much broader sequence of events and does not reflect the full circumstances surrounding the incident, during which the young player had been subjected to repeated behaviour that caused him significant distress.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job READ MORE :

"Wolves staff are disappointed by those continuing to share the footage in question and condemn, in the strongest possible terms, those who have sought to identify, threaten and abuse the young person involved. Instances of extreme abuse and threats have already been shared with police."

‌



A one-minute clip of the fight showed a boy wearing official England training gear grab a phone from another boy who was lying on the bed of a hotel room. The two can be seen grappling over the phone before punches and kicks were thrown.

The boy who tried to take the phone then attempts to put the other in a headlock. He subsequently dragged him around the room before throwing him on the floor.

In the statement, Wolves academy director Jonathan Hunter-Barrett added: "Whilst the academy does not condone violence under any circumstances, it is important to recognise that this footage captures only the final moments of a much longer sequence of events. It does not reflect the repeated behaviour this young player had been subjected to, the significant distress he had experienced beforehand, or the circumstances that led to the incident.

‌



"Those of us who know this young man understand that the footage is not an accurate reflection of either his character or the circumstances he found himself in. He is respectful, humble and has consistently demonstrated the standards and values we expect from our academy players, earning the respect of both staff and teammates through the way he conducts himself every day.

Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months READ MORE :

Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

"Like all young people, Academy players learn and develop through both positive and difficult experiences. We are incredibly proud of the person he is today, and of the way he has responded to this distressing incident and the subsequent attention it has received, both when the footage first emerged in 2025 and again in recent days.

"This has been an extremely difficult period for him and his family. Our priority is their welfare, and we will continue to provide them with the care and support they need.

‌



"We would also encourage people to consider the impact of sharing and commenting on footage involving minors and young people. Behind every video is a person and a family, and their wellbeing should always be at the forefront of our minds.

"As a club, we do not tolerate bullying, intimidation or abuse in any form. Supporting and protecting the welfare of our young people will always be our priority, and our commitment is to continue supporting young players in their development, both as footballers and, more importantly, as people."

Sports.title: Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen
Sports.content:
Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen

Vinicius Jr has been linked with a sensational move to the Premier League to join Arsenal

View 2 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Spanish media have given their say on the possibility of Vinicius Jr joining Arsenal. The Real Madrid winger is wanted by the Gunners but talks between the clubs have yet to begin.

‌



The 26-year-old is in the final 12 months of his contract and if Real can't secure an extension, they could be open to selling in order to avoid losing him for free next summer. A number of Spanish newspapers have weighed in on whether the transfer could actually happen.

‌



Sport claims that Real president Florentino Perez has set a non-negotiable fee of £136million (€160m). The media outlet understands that the club will not bat an eyelid at a figure below this for Vini's signature.

‌



Real are considering this fee to be an initial purchase with a number of add-ons, including performance bonuses and trophies won. Should Arsenal meet these demands, Sport sees no reason as to how the deal couldn't go through.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

Arsenal have trump card to beat Man Utd in £40m Ollie Watkins transfer race READ MORE :

Marca aren't as confident that the transfer will happen though. The Spanish newspaper states that Vini is demanding at least £25m (€30m) per season to bring his salary close to Kylian Mbappe's.

They believe the contract extension negotiations are entering a "delicate phase" and if these conditions aren't met, it is unclear what the future holds for the winger. Cadena SER believes that the arrival of Yan Diomande could be the end of Vini in Spain.

View 2 Images Vini Jr wants a similar salary to Kylian Mbappe (Image: Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The media outlet claims that Real's pursuit of the Ivory Coast international showcases the club's movement into a new era. The La Liga giants saw a £85.4m bid rejected by RB Leipzig and are now submitting an improved offer, believing that a deal can be done.

The pair would be competing for the left wing spot and Real's growing interest in Diomande is a hint to the media that Vini Jr is on his way out. They did admit that there is a world where both wingers remain in Spain but Vini's recent links to Arsenal could mean the 19-year-old is his replacement under Jose Mourinho.

Sports.title: Greaves beats Sherrock to claim record third Women's Matchplay crown
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves won the Women's World Matchplay for a record third time with a 6-5 last-leg victory over Fallon Sherrock at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool.

After Sherrock forced the contest to go all the way, Greaves came through clutch with a 180 then 145 to leave 56 for the match. She pinned that on D10 to seal victory once again.

The win adds to Greaves' 2023 and 2024 triumphs in this tournament. It was Sherrock that Greaves met in the 2024 Women's Matchplay final in which Greaves took the spoils in a 6-3 win.

It adds to an already impressive year for 'Beau and Arrow' in which she became the first woman to win a Pro Tour event at Players Championship 11. She also hit a nine-darter on the Tour and became the first woman to qualify for the European Tour.

Sports.title: Norris wins first race of 2026 as Hamilton suffers more penalty pain
Sports.content:
Lando Norris won his first race of 2026 after an early squabble with McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Pole-sitter Norris lost out to Piastri in a feisty opening lap but eventually used his stronger pace to retake the lead after the second round of pit stops, as Piastri made contact when lapping Williams' Carlos Sainz.

However, Piastri later retired when running in second due to a gearbox issue which caused a late Virtual Safety Car with 14 laps remaining.

Ferrari elected to pit Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc from second and fifth but it turned out to be the wrong call for Hamilton as he sped in the pit lane, so was given a five-second time penalty, and could not overtake Max Verstappen or Kimi Antonelli who both did not pit.

Verstappen hung onto second after a stunning final stint as Antonelli fended Hamilton off on the track to extend his championship lead to 50 points over the Ferrari driver and 59 points to George Russell, who stalled at the start then fought back to seventh.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Hamilton's penalty demoted him to fifth behind Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar finished sixth.

The seven-time world champion will rue another missed opportunity to challenge for the win as Ferrari did not optimise their strategy and he lost time early on when battling Verstappen, who made a great move on Hamilton into Turn 1.

Racing Bulls duo Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad had a race-long scrap with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg with Lawson coming out on top from Hulkenberg and Lindblad in the final points-paying positions in the last Grand Prix before the four-week summer break.

Hungarian GP Result: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) George Russell, Mercedes



8) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



9) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



10) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls

Norris wins after early team orders dispute

McLaren's big upgrade package for Hungary vaulted them to the front and Norris had been in flying form throughout the weekend.

But, Piastri got a tremendous start and capitalised on a wide moment from Norris at the second turn to take the lead and claim track position on a circuit which is tricky to overtake at.

Norris clearly had more pace in hand but was unable to find a way through and became increasingly frustrated on the radio, asking if he could pit first before the second round of pit stops.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Oscar Piastri take the lead from Lando Norris as George Russell has a race start to forget at Hungaroring in Budapest

The reigning world champion was told he could not, so McLaren pitted Piastri just before half distance of the 70-lap Hungarian Grand Prix while Norris stayed out.

Despite having old tyres, Norris was able to slightly outpace Piastri who got caught out by lapped traffic, including Sainz who did not see the Australian at Turn 2 so the pair made minor contact.

Norris pitted on Lap 40 and came out ahead of his team-mate and went on to dominate the remainder of the race, while Piastri was on course for second, only to suffer a gearbox failure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri has a technical failure and stops out on track in Budapest

"My pace today was probably some of the best pace I've ever had. The car was beautiful to drive and I felt very confident, so a great race," said Norris.

"And to get it back in terms of going long, which is certainly not what I was expecting, but the pace was so good I could always extend the stints, and fresh tyres then always won me the race."

Missed chance for Ferrari and Hamilton?

Having qualified on the front row on a track Ferrari were expected to be strong at, things looked promising for Hamilton at the end of Q3 only for him to be demoted three places for impeding Piastri in qualifying.

Nevertheless, starting fifth, there were still opportunities for Hamilton and he made a strong start on his new softs to move into fourth, crucially ahead of team-mate Leclerc.

He was all over arch-rival Verstappen during the first stint but could not make an overtake, so Ferrari pitted him early to undercut the four-time world champion.

Image: Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton battling at the Hungarian GP (AP Photo/Darko Bandic)

It paid off, only for Verstappen to make a stunning move down the inside at Turn 1 after a blistering out lap so Hamilton was stuck behind the Red Bull driver again.

He pitted for a second time on Lap 30 and was on a charge, effectively in third place behind Norris and Piastri as Red Bull chose to run Verstappen long.

After Piastri's retirement, Hamilton was on course for second and to make inroads into his championship deficit to Antonelli but Ferrari, with hindsight, made the wrong decision to pit the British driver under a late Virtual Safety Car.

Image: Lewis Hamilton now trails Kimi Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship (Getty Images)

Hamilton dropped from second to fourth, just behind Antonelli on a close pit merge but was deemed to speed in the pit lane.

He couldn't find a way by Antonelli and his five-second time penalty for speeding dropped him to fifth on a day Ferrari probably had the pace to at least fight Norris for the win.

Sports.title: Sooryavanshi stars again as India knock England off top spot in T20I rankings
Sports.content:
Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struck his second fifty in three innings as India sealed a 3-0 T20I sweep of Zimbabwe to knock England off top spot in the rankings.

Sooryavanshi's 81 from 49 balls in Harare featured four sixes and eight fours and followed his maiden half-century for his country - a 19-ball 50 - in Thursday's series opener at the same venue.

The left-hander - who lit up the 2026 IPL with 776 runs in 16 matches for Rajasthan Royals at a remarkable strike-rate of 237.30 - first played senior cricket for India during the recent 4-0 T20 thrashing in England, registering scores of 14, 13 and 15.

Score summary - Zimbabwe vs India, third T20I, Harare India 192-5 from 20 overs (elected to bat): Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (81 off 49 balls), Ishan Kishan (29 off 26), Shreyas Iyer (27 off 18), Rinku Singh (25no off 14); Brad Evans (2-41) Zimbabwe 157-7 from 20 overs (target 193): Ryan Burl (54no off 43), Wesley Madhevere (28 off 25); Mayank Yadav (3-29), Shardul Thakur (2-45) India sweep three-match series 3-0.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sooryavanshi was twice dismissed by Jofra during India's 4-0 T20 drubbing in England, including for 15 in the penultimate match in Bristol

India's heavy defeat in the UK had seen Harry Brook's men overtake them as the No 1 T20I team before they returned to the summit after seizing a 2-0 lead against Zimbabwe.

They would have slipped back to second had they lost the finale but ran out 35-run winners despite some sloppy fielding.

Sooryavanhsi's innings - which ended when he was superbly caught by a diving Brad Evans - propelled Shreyas Iyer's side to 192-5 and Zimbabwe could only make 157-7 in reply, with Ryan Burl (54no off 43) top-scoring.

Image: Sooryavanshi (left) shared half-century stands with Ishan Kishan (right) and India captain Shreyas Iyer on Sunday

India are next in action in August as they visit Sri Lanka for a two-match Test series, before returning to white-ball cricket across September and October when they host West Indies for three one-day internationals and five T20 internationals.

England will look to move back top of the T20I standings when they welcome Sri Lanka for three fixtures from September 15.

The series opener is at the Utilita Bowl in Southampton before further games at Sophia Gardens in Cardiff (September 17) and Emirates Old Trafford in Manchester (September 19) ahead of a three-match ODI series between the sides.

Like India, England also play Test cricket next, with the first of three red-ball clashes against Pakistan starting at Headingley on August 19, live on Sky Sports and contract-free with NOW.

Sports.title: Shin stutters to win in Scotland as players prepare for Women's Open
Sports.content:
Jenny Shin stuttered over the line at the ISPS HANDA Women's Scottish Open to secure her first LPGA Tour title in a decade with England's defending champion Lottie Woad finishing tied-37th as players prepared for next week's AIG Women's Open.

South Korean golfer Shin ended two strokes clear of compatriot A-Lim Kim on nine under par after bogeying two of her final three holes on Sunday to sign for a three-over 75, having begun round four with a five-shot advantage over Thailand's Pajaree Anannarukarn.

The 33-year-old suffered three bogeys in a row from the sixth but her birdies at 10 and 12 proved crucial following her sluggish end to the round as Kim's four-under 68 came in vain at Dundonald Links.

Shin was emotional as she clinched her first trophy since the Volunteers of America Texas Shootout in May 2016 - she is the first woman in 30 years to go a full decade between LPGA Tour wins - and can now switch focus to the major at Royal Lytham and St Annes.

She said: "My first title didn't really feel like a win at the time. I didn't feel like I deserved it. It felt very accidental. But this one definitely feels a lot different, feels like I earned it. I worked hard for it."

Image: Lottie Woad finished tied-37th in her Scottish Open title defence

How did the British and Irish stars fare?

Woad - whose victory in Ayrshire last year was her first as a pro and came a few weeks after she had won the Women's Irish Open as an amateur - closed out her week with a one-over 73 to finish on seven over, with most of the damage done by a six-over 78 on Saturday.

Charley Hull, who started her tournament with a 78, ended up in a share of 44th place on 10 over after shooting 74 on Sunday.

Image: England's Charley Hull finished 10 over for the tournament in Ayrshire

Ireland's Leona Maguire claimed a top-10 finish on one under after a final-round 70 took her into the red, with Alice Hewson, on three over, the highest-placed British golfer in a share of 19th spot.

What about some of the other big names?

Reigning Women's Open champion Miyu Yamashita - who triumphed by two strokes from fellow Japanese Minami Katsu and England's Hull at Royal Porthcawl in 2025 - finished tied-fifth on three under in Scotland ahead of her title defence in Lancashire from Thursday.

Image: World No 1 Nelly Korda has won two majors this year, the Chevron Championship and the US Women's Open

World No 1 Nelly Korda will be aiming for a third major title of the year and fifth of her career after victories at the Chevron Championship and US Women's Open this term.

The American will head to Royal Lytham & St Annes following a finish of tied-16th at the Scottish Open, shooting her best round of the week on Sunday - a three-under 69 - to end on two over par.

This year's other double major winner - Women's PGA and Evian champion Haeran Ryu - did not play at the Scottish Open.

Sports.title: England 'far off their best' in netball defeat to Australia in Glasgow
Sports.content:
England suffered their first defeat of the Commonwealth Games after going down 66-47 to reigning champions Australia in Glasgow.

The Vitality Roses trailed 18-11 after the first quarter and 35-24 at half-time before a series of handling errors helped Australia stretch their lead to 56-35 with 15 minutes left.

England won the final quarter 12-10 but the damage was already done as they were unable to back up their opening 83-34 victory over Northern Ireland on Saturday.

England, for whom Olivia Tchine scored 23 goals, face Malawi on Monday before further Group A games against Tonga on Wednesday and South Africa on Thursday.

The top two sides in Groups A and B after all the sides have played the others in their pool once each will advance to the semi-finals.

Image: Australia are two from two in Glasgow after also beating Tonga on Saturday

Williams says England can take lessons from defeat

The Vitality Roses took Commonwealth Games gold on the Gold Coast in 2018, beating host nation Australia in the final, but did not medal in Birmingham four years ago.

Speaking after Sunday's defeat to Australia's Diamonds, England captain Fran Williams said lessons would be learned: "That's definitely not the result that we came for but it's also not the performance.

"We were far off our best and never really got momentum. It's really tough when a game blows out like that in the second half.

"You've got to make sure that you're still going after those small wins and little fights. That's why I'm so proud of the last 15 minutes in terms of getting a quarter win at the end when it was tough.

"It's great we've had that exposure against a team that's probably setting the standard in the competition. We've got the learning from the experience so we can move on.

"There's no point dwelling on it. It's about taking what we need from it and bringing it into [the Malawi match]. That will help us drop any disappointment. You've got to look forward."

Sports.title: Fury vs Joshua: Everything you need to know
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua both won over the weekend to keep themselves on course for a blockbuster heavyweight showdown – here is everything you need to know about the proposed fight.

Fury and Joshua have shared eras, headlines and negotiating tables without ever sharing a ring. A fight was previously announced for August 2021 in Saudi Arabia and terms were accepted again for a December 2022 date before both collapsed without a punch being thrown.

This weekend's return to the ring for both men is expected to be the final box-ticking exercise before it happens for real this time.

What happened in Fury and AJ's warm-up fights?

Fury claimed a seventh-round TKO over Mariusz Wach at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Thailand on Friday, with Wach signalling to his corner to wave the fight off before the officials ended it ahead of the eighth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dev Sahni reveals how Tyson Fury toppled Mariusz Wach in a non-TV fight in Thailand

The bout was not televised and fought in front of around 1,500 spectators in Pattaya and was the 37-year-old Fury's second since ending his latest retirement, following his points win over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

Joshua's night in Jeddah was far more dramatic. He was floored inside 20 seconds by Kristian Prenga, hit the canvas twice in the first round, then knocked out the Albanian with right hands in the second.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment Anthony Joshua sealed victory over Kristian Prenga with a huge second round knockout (Courtesy of DAZN)

It was AJ's first outing since he was a passenger in a December car crash that killed his friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele and his first fight since stopping Jake Paul last December.

When will the pair fight?

The calendar has been circled for November and the warm-up double-header was arranged to align with that timeline.

Contracts are signed and the pair are now set to meet, though a precise date has not been announced – although Fury said after beating Wach that he hopes the fight is signed "next week".

Where will the fight be?

No venue has been announced.

Turki Alalshikh, who is promoting the fight, has said he wants the fight to suit a global audience and that he will talk to London authorities over a later-than-usual start time.

Sky Sports revealed, though, that Brent Council had not yet been contacted about extending Wembley Stadium's usual 11pm curfew.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has revealed that the USA is now the preferred venue for Alalshikh, but highlighted that the current signed contracts state that the fight must be in the UK.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn hit back at Fury's claims he was worried about a potential bout against AJ falling through

"That doesn't tally up with the contract that we signed," he said. "Until we're happy, we expect every point of that contract to be followed. I feel like this fight should be taking place in the UK.

"If they want to change the contract, then we have to renegotiate the contract. Which, by the way, is not a problem but it's a conversation we have to have."

Wembley has been championed by Barry Hearn, Eddie's dad, while Cardiff's Principality Stadium has been rumoured but Croke Park appears not to be an option despite earlier suggestions of talks about moving the bout to Dublin.

"There's two or three different places it could be but there's still objections to a few of them and the one man who's going to make the decisions is Turki Alalshikh, and Netflix," said Spencer Brown, Fury's manager.

"They're going to make the decisions. They both want the fight, so there's going to be a bit of chopping and changing."

What has AJ said?

"I am going to rip his heart out," Joshua said after beating Prenga. "All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now.

"I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat."

He also dedicated the win on Saturday to his late friends, adding: "It's more than just punch power, it was spirit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Anthony Joshua dedicates his win over Kristian Prenga to his late friends who died in December's car crash (Courtesy of DAZN)

Joshua has also insisted the contract states the fight must be in the UK.

What has Fury said?

Fury got his shots in after beating Wach and questioned whether Joshua has the "guts" to face him, referencing his rival declining to enter the ring after the Makhmudov fight in front of 70,000 at Tottenham.

"The biggest test of it all is how big his ***** are," said Fury.

"I think he's a big s********. In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me.

"Let's see if he ever does, I'm not convinced."

Fury then reeled off Vegas, New York, Ireland, London, Belfast and even Pattaya as possible venues.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spencer Brown says Tyson Fury's presence at ringside for Joshua vs Prenga was never discussed and he's not convinced AJ will be in favour of fighting The Gypsy King in New York

That followed his Sky Sports News interview in fight week, where he said "I don't care if I ever see him again in my life" and vowed not to travel to Saudi Arabia for a face-off.

Despite voicing his concerns, Fury did say he hopes the next big fight is signed next week and his management confirmed that they are looking to definitely get it done within the next fortnight.

"When the fight is announced, which we anticipate we will do in the next couple of weeks," said Brown. "There's still a couple of contractual things that we need to get through, i.e. where it's going to be, when it's going to be, how it's going to be, but I've been assured that we'll be sorting it out in the next couple of weeks."

Who is the favourite according to the experts?

Former middleweight world title contender Matthew Macklin believes that the 'Gypsy King' is the clear favourite.

"I think Tyson Fury is favourite," said Macklin. "I think because he's got a style and assets that age better. I think AJ is more athletic but as you get older those athletic qualities diminish.

"I think his punch resistance probably has gone now. Dubois, it was a bad knockout, and he's had that fight against Jake Paul since.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn backs Anthony Joshua to beat Tyson Fury when the British rivals finally meet later this year, insisting Wembley Stadium is the ideal venue for fans.

"I don't think his punch resistance will be anywhere near what it once was, and also his reflexes won't be what they were, so it's like a double whammy.

"Fury, his reflexes won't be what they were either so it's not like it's all AJ on the decline. He's not the fighter he was. Neither of them were, but I think we all know that and accept that.

"It's still a level playing field because they're both past their best, so it's still going to be an intriguing battle."

As for Sky Sports Boxing expert and former WBO Cruiserweight champion Johnny Nelson, he said: "There's a word called 'mercurial' and that describes Anthony Joshua.

"He's got so much talent but it's a case of which version of him turns up on performance night.

"The talented fighter we know, he wasn't there [on Saturday]. The guts, the heart, he was there, because after 20 seconds he got put down and had to get back up again. He was still making rookie mistakes. I'm thinking, you shouldn't make those mistakes at this stage in your career.

"Listen, I'm an AJ fan, but I'd have to lean towards Tyson Fury's fluidity, his boxing ability – because of that vulnerability from Anthony Joshua, getting caught by that sneaky little uppercut on the inside, getting caught again.

"These are natural shots from Tyson Fury. When it comes to heart, determination, desire and want, I put that in the corner of Anthony Joshua.

"But on last night's performance and on Friday night's performance, I'd have to lean towards Tyson Fury, from what I've seen."

What next?

The date and venue announcement is the key piece of outstanding information but, given the November window, that confirmation is expected within weeks.

For reference, tickets for Joshua's fight with Dubois went on sale a little under three months before that event.

The plan once both men came through the weekend was a joint press conference to formally announce the fight, though Fury's refusal to share a stage with Joshua makes the shape of that uncertain and there is also the venue conundrum to answer.

Fury expects a signing within days before fans can look forward to what will be one of the most eagerly awaited British boxing matches of all time.
