Sports.title: ‘We want to win the league’: Arsenal’s new recruits ink in WSL success
Sports.content:
Georgia Stanway looks at her arms and then down at her legs on day one of Arsenal’s pre-season. “As you can see, I’m covered in tattoos,” she says. “I only see the bare skin, the space, so I need to keep collecting more”.

Tattooing and being tattooed is her creative outlet, her way of expressing herself off the pitch. But seeing space is key to the 27‑year‑old England midfielder being exceptional on the pitch.

Stanway’s unveiling video, after her move from Bayern Munich, showed a delicate, cursive script reading “whatever the weather” tattooed on her arm. It was a bold statement to get the lyric from North London Forever, Arsenal’s anthem, etched into her skin before she has stepped on to the Emirates Stadium pitch in red and white. “It shows I’m going to give absolutely everything for this club. I want to hit the ground running, play my game, connect with my teammates, connect with the fans and look forward to an exciting future at the club.”

Stanway is emblematic of Arsenal’s summer of change, one of seven signings so far. Meanwhile, Lotte Wubben-Moy, a lifelong fan who joined Arsenal’s academy at 13, represents the core and culture that is a point of focus at the club. It is a culture players want to be a part of, so much so it leads to players getting a tattoo on day one of being there. “She has set a very high bar,” says Wubben-Moy, with a grin. “That’s Georgia. She goes all in and I like that.”

Wubben-Moy is ready to stake a claim in Arsenal’s starting XI after struggling to nail down a position in defence despite having performed exceptionally well when covering for injured players. “I’ve always felt ready,” says the 27-year-old. “When I get my moment, I deliver. Historically, as a club, we’re built on defensive solidity. If we have a solid defence, it allows us to create and score. That should be the stepping stone towards victories. So I will continue to contribute to the defensive solidity in whatever way, shape or form that is. But I want my spot.”

View image in fullscreen Lotte Wubben-Moy lifts the Champions Cup trophy during the Arsenal trophy parade in May. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

There was widespread recognition that Arsenal’s squad needed a revamp, that the age needed to be lowered and changes made if they were going to take the next step. That meant big names leaving, most notably Beth Mead and Katie McCabe. “They’re both absolute legends of the game and we have so much respect for them,” says Jodie Taylor, the former Arsenal striker who became the club’s technical director in January. “But we always knew this window was going to come with some changes.”

“Change is inevitable in women’s football,” says Wubben-Moy. “If you speak to a player and they don’t say they’re nimble, you’ve got someone that’s not built for the game. We’ve become a nimble team, a team that can move with the ebb and flow of women’s football.

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead left in a busy summer for Arsenal. Photograph: Rhianna Chadwick/PA

“That’s not just within the playing group, it’s something replicated within the staff, the boardroom, the commercial team, the comms team. Everyone is so willing to move and to dictate what we want.

“If you’d asked me about change four or five years ago, I’d have been a bit intimidated, but now I know what to do and I’m part of the driver of it. The opportunity we have and that I see for us as a team, as a collective, is something that really excites me.”

Arsenal’s approach to Stanway’s recruitment was a contributing factor to her wanting to join the club. “Arsenal came in early doors,” she says. “I really enjoyed they were super loyal from the beginning and wanted me even when I wasn’t available. It’s nice feeling being wanted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The last four years in Munich were unbelievable, but I knew I wanted to take the next step and I felt at Arsenal there was an opportunity for me to be able to progress, to make my game better and to play with world-class players.”

Arsenal have done most of their business early, with Stanway joined by experienced internationals Selina Çerçi, Géraldine Reuteler, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez, as well as young talents Lisa Baum and Isabella Damm. No major international tournament and seven signings in for day one of pre-season is a big boost for Renée Slegers and her coaching staff, particularly after two seasons of slow starts to domestic campaigns.

“The market is not easy, though, it’s constantly changing and the pool of elite talent is small and several clubs are fishing from it,” says Taylor. “You try and plan as much as you can, but you also have to be reactive in the market. We’re always trying to keep an eye on the future, but we have to be quite agile.

“We can talk about positional needs, qualities, ages and succession planning, but if a player’s not available or they just don’t exist, it can be like trying to fit square pegs and round holes. As well as looking at current needs and positional profiles, we talk a lot about our core style of play, but we also want to play with variety, be unpredictable and have different qualities in players too.”

View image in fullscreen Former Arsenal striker Jodie Taylor, now technical director, is leading the strong recruitment this summer. Photograph: Zuma Press/Alamy

The players that have come in have brought energy, says Wubben-Moy, who was on an emotional rollercoaster during Arsenal’s men’s Premier League and women’s Champions Cup-winning parade, with the bus looping past Highbury Corner, where she filmed her contract renewal video, and past Islington town hall, where she got married to cyclist Tao Geoghegan Hart a few weeks later.

“I like to focus on what they’re entering, which is a culture that has been created by history, by players and staff that are the core of this team and who have all lived through the changes to different degrees: Kelly [Smith], Renée, myself, Leah [Williamson], Kim [Little], Jodie, too. We’ve been privy to lots of different things all of us are holding on to and releasing, in a healthy way, the things we know we need to. It’s efficient, we’re focused, we know what we do next.

“It’s like you’re cooking the most beautiful recipe and then you add the final small ingredients that make the marginal difference, that elevate, and you create something that’s beautiful and that you can relish and enjoy. That’s what we’re in the process of now with a beautiful long pre-season. I’m desperate to get it out of the way so we can then serve what we’re cooking to the fans and be like: ‘Let’s eat and we’ll all eat together for the whole year.’”

The average attendance of more than 34,000 fans for WSL games at the Emirates last season and the club’s pioneering history in women’s football, as well as Champions League win in 2025, are huge selling points, and all concerned at Arsenal want more, including a first Women’s Super League title since 2019.

“We’re in a great place,” says Taylor. “But we would have liked to have won more trophies last season and that is our huge ambition coming into this year. I’ll flat out say it: we want to win the league. We are an ambitious club and with the signings we’ve made we feel like we’re in a great place to do that.”

Sports.title: How the death of Jayden Adams shook a community: ‘Being on the pitch was his happy place’
Sports.content:
For Jayden Adams, the South Africa midfielder who died this month at the age of 25, football was a “safe space”. Those words, used by Adams’s junior coach Steve Barker at his memorial service 10 days ago, tell you everything you need to know about his life beyond the pitch.

Adams’s battles were bestowed on him almost from birth. Though he was born into newly democratic South Africa, by the early 2000s the revolution was well on its way to being betrayed. The vote was extended to all, but few could make full use of the freedoms available to them because socioeconomic circumstances in the country had barely changed. Stellenbosch, where the Adams family were based, is a perfect example.

Its facade is a tourist dream: a university town nestled among vineyards, Cape Dutch architecture and indie boutiques. Most visitors never venture beyond the town centre or into its suburbs, which are home to the far less privileged and are havens of neglect. Those areas are classic apartheid hangovers, where the wealth has been preserved for a historically advantaged elite and those on the margins, working-class communities of people of colour, are all but invisible.

Ironically, that is how Adams is most often described. He moved in the shadows, both of society and the sport in which he excelled. “Jayden was a guy of very few words. He was quiet, very shy and the smallest among his teammates,” Brendine Johnson, an Adams family spokesperson, says. “Initially, a lot of people missed his football qualities because of his size, but he had a very good fighting spirit. It just wasn’t always on display.”

Adams loved the game dearly and his aunt Monica Thaoge recalled how, as a child, he would kick anything round – “even onions” she said at his memorial. His parents, Juanito and Candice, previously mentioned potatoes as their son’s football of choice. Nobody in the family talks about lacking in financial means because theirs was a community striving to make life better. But there were absences, especially early on.

View image in fullscreen Members of the Mamelodi Sundowns football club carry Jayden Adams’ coffin at the funeral service for the player on Saturday. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters

“Everybody in areas like that is just trying to make ends meet,” says Roger Telemachus, the former South Africa cricketer who grew up on the same street as Adams’s father in Cloetesville. “For the kids, they may not have noticed so much because they were occupied, mostly with playing sport. Some fathers, like Juanito, really encouraged their kids and everyone used to play everything on the street: tennis, football, rugby, cricket. It was also the best way of staying out of trouble.”

Problems were there for everyone to see and, according to Telemachus, have got worse “in the last 20 years”. They include gangsterism, substance abuse and crimes that range from petty to serious. Adams was able to escape from that life when he moved to the slightly more affluent area of Ida’s Valley, but still he did not have a life of luxury. For a period, the family of six, which included four children, lived in a two-bedroom place. At other times, they were with his maternal grandmother, Marianna. “He basically grew up in her yard,” says Johnson.

Things started to change for Adams when he was picked for the Stellenbosch Academy Under-18 side at the age of 15. “The environment was tough, especially if you are not big or tall enough, but when physicality was no longer the most important thing, people saw that Jayden was technically very good,” says Johnson.

His coaches agree. Barker, the nephew of South Africa’s Afcon winning coach, Clive, and the current coach of Simba in Tanzania, gave an emotional assessment of Adams’s skills shortly after his death. “You get many good footballers but you get few great footballers. Jayden was great,” he told Newzroom Afrika.

“Jayden had three attributes that set him apart: an incredible first touch, his weight of pass – I’ve never seen anything like it – and he loved the game so much. Being on the pitch was his happy place. He didn’t pass the ball, he used to caress the ball. He was special and his football intelligence was just outstanding.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams played in South Africa’s World Cup group game against Czechia despite the death of his grandmother the day before. Photograph: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

It was under Barker that Adams blossomed. He became the first player from the Stellenbosch Academy to play in South Africa’s top flight, the Premier Soccer League. Five years and an international call up later, the country’s richest club, Mamelodi Sundowns, came calling. This year, at the start of his second season with them, Adams shaved his head, in what he joked was a sign of maturity and called himself a “grootman” (big man). The nickname stuck.

Adams never said it, but he may also have realised how much he had grown up. By then, he had been picked, played for and dropped from the national side after arriving late at a training camp and irking the head coach, Hugo Broos. He had also lost two of his academy teammates, including a close friend.

In February 2023, Oshwin Andries, who was 19, died from stabbing injuries he sustained in Paarl, which is 16km north of Stellenbosch. Three years later, Jeandre Gaffoor, 20, drowned in the Krom River.

When Sundowns won the CAF Champions League in May, Adams dedicated his medal to Andries. To lose so much has weighed on the town, but through Adams they have had reason to celebrate.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Members of Adams’s family, including his father, Juanito (centre left), and mother, Candice (centre right), at his memorial service last week. Photograph: Rodger Bosch/AFP/Getty Images

His role in Sundowns’ continental victory and a call-up to the World Cup squad suggested Adams’s career trajectory was rising. After a first season at Sundowns when he was often playing off the bench and his place in the side was questioned, he had become integral to the team. At Adams’s memorial, the Sundowns senior coach, Steve Komphela, called him “the heart of our team and the heartbeat of our playing style” who “understood the game like a coach and played it as a player”.

In the past year, Adams was playing to the potential people who knew him well had seen years ago and surprising others with his courage and drive to succeed. South Africa’s captain, Ronwen Williams, recalled an incident at this year’s Africa Cup of Nations when the tiny Adams took on a tall Mali opponent with some choice local words. Williams asked Adams if he knew the size of the player he was sledging, but Adams shrugged it off and replied that the Malian wouldn’t understand anyway.

“That was the character he had,” Williams said at the memorial, smiling through his tears as he bade farewell to the teammate he called “my ma se kind” (my mother’s child, a term of endearment used in South Africa).

As his star rose, Adams was careful not to advertise his achievements. “Jayden knew what he had, but he never wanted to voice it. He was very competitive, but he would never brag,” says Johnson. “You get people who are very good verbally on social media. Jayden was not like that. And he wanted to give back. After every game, he would be giving away shirts and boots to kids who asked.”

He also concentrated on providing for his family because he “always promised them he would change their financial situation”.

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams signs a South Africa shirt for a young Mexican fan who arrived at the team’s World Cup hotel. ‘He wanted to give back.’ Photograph: SAFA

At the World Cup, Adams played for them, even through immense pain. His grandmother Marianna died the day before South Africa’s match against Czechia and Adams opted to remain with the squad. He played that match and appeared in good spirits afterwards and called the 1-1 draw positive, even if he was feeling the opposite way.

He also played the next game against South Korea, which South Africa won to reach the knockouts for the first time. Post-game footage showed him sitting on his own while the rest of the squad celebrated with a signature song and dance.

At the memorial, Komphela offered the Adams family a Bible verse as a comfort, but it may as well be a summary. Psalm 23:4: “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.”

They will know Adams took that walk many times over his short life and he did not fear. He leaves behind his parents, three siblings, a partner, two children and a community who have gone through what no neighbourhood should. In all that, he has gone from not wanting to be known, to entering the footballing world’s spotlight. A minute’s silence was observed at several World Cup games in Adams’s memory. That is not the way his family would have pictured him coming to global attention, but it has shown them that, in football, he was always far more valued than anyone thought.

“I don’t think the community knew how big he was and how people enjoyed his football,” says Johnson. “It’s a huge shock.”

Sports.title: Inter enter talks with Tottenham over signing captain Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Inter have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of Cristian Romero. The Spurs captain helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final this month, but could leave this summer for a significant fee after an eventful five-year spell.

The centre-back has made 156 appearances since he joined Tottenham in 2021 and guided the club to Europa League success last year, but served four separate suspensions during a difficult 2025-26 campaign.

With Jan Paul van Hecke signed for £52m from Brighton and Marcos Senesi joining as a free agent in June to boost the defensive options of Roberto De Zerbi’s side, Spurs will let Romero depart and his representatives have been in Milan for talks with Inter this weekend.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilo, told Sky Italy: “It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.”

Sports.title: Liverpool start Iraola era in style to beat Sunderland but Gomez injury deepens defensive worries
Sports.content:
The Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool opened with victory over Sunderland in Nashville – and a deepening of concerns over the defensive options at his disposal. The sight of Joe Gomez hobbling off after 10 minutes of the new head coach’s first game and two teenagers forming a raw partnership in the centre of defence in his absence intensified the spotlight on a department in need of work.

Liverpool had few issues at the other end of the pitch against Régis Le Bris’s side, who were resplendent in pink in Tennessee, where second-half finishes from Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas delivered an ultimately comfortable win.

“Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe,” said Iraola, who will have been impressed by lively displays from Calum Scanlon, Kieran Morrison and Koumas. “We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we’ve lost Joe straight away.”

Geodis Park paid tribute to the late Kevin Keegan before kick-off on Saturday, with both sets of supporters applauding the Liverpool, Hamburg and Newcastle great prior to observing an impeccable period of silence in his memory. The crowd itself was sparse, with plenty of empty seats in the 30,000 capacity stadium, although the official attendance was given as 24,897. Charging from $129 to $392 (£96 to £292) for tickets to a pre-season friendly missing its contingent of World Cup players perhaps explains why.

Sunderland were without Granit Xhaka, Brian Brobbey and summer signing Thomas Meunier. Liverpool’s absentee list included World Cup finalists Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Muñoz, along with Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch, who will join the tour next week, and Virgil van Dijk, Cody Gakpo and Alisson, who will resume pre-season training next week but back on Merseyside.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola sent on Federico Chiesa, who put Liverpool 3-2 ahead. Photograph: Andrew J Clark/ISI Photos/Getty Images

Liverpool also had a summer signing missing. Jérémy Jacquet, who was acquired for an initial £55m from Rennes, was left out as a precaution but is expected to feature before the tour concludes against Leeds in Chicago on Sunday.

“With Jérémy we decided to take it easy with him,” Iraola explained. “He’s had a lot of months without playing, he’s been training very well, but we’re going to take it easy with him. He will play probably in the last game of this US tour, he will have time to have minutes.”

View image in fullscreen Joe Gomez is helped by trainers after going down early with an injury. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Having expressed worry over his “very thin” defensive options earlier in the week, Iraola’s resources were stretched further when Gomez went down injured early on. The luckless Gomez was unable to continue after treatment and his departure meant Liverpool’s central defence comprised two 18-year-olds recruited in January, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe. Kostas Tsimikas took the captain’s armband from Gomez, then passed it on to Szoboszlai when he was replaced at the interval. Talla Ndiaye, a £1m signing from Amitié in Senegal, and Ndukwe, a £2.5m transfer from Austria Vienna who teamed up with Liverpool only this summer, reflect the club’s policy of recruiting central defenders for the future.

The here and now, however, must also be addressed. With Ibrahima Konaté joining Real Madrid, Giovanni Leoni yet to resume full training after his anterior cruciate ligament injury, Gomez injury-prone and Jacquet untested in the Premier League, though rated extremely highly, the responsibility on Van Dijk will be considerable next season. As it was last season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The answer to the future quiz question of who scored the first goal of the Iraola era at Liverpool is Morrison. The 19-year-old winger started on the right, also known as the chasm left by Mohamed Salah, and slid a fine finish into the far corner of Melker Ellborg’s goal when released inside the area by Harvey Elliott, another player desperate to impress the new Liverpool head coach after a wasted season on loan at Aston Villa.

View image in fullscreen Jaydon Jones and Timur Tutierov combined for a Sunderland goal. Photograph: Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images

Sunderland equalised in style when Enzo Le Fée broke from midfield and swept a superb shot into Giorgi Mamardashvili’s top corner from 25 yards. Le Bris made 10 changes at half-time, Iraola five, and Sunderland soon took the lead when Jaydon Jones picked out Timur Tutierov inside the area and the striker slotted into the net from 12 yards.

Szoboszlai gave the majority of the crowd what they had paid good money to see when controlling a loose Sunderland clearance 22 yards out and beating Ellborg with a convincing finish. Chiesa steered a clever shot inside the near post from Calvin Ramsay’s pass behind the Sunderland defence before Koumas, released by Szoboszlai, sealed the win.

Sports.title: Tottenham begin tour with victory over Auckland FC in front of record crowd
Sports.content:
Dane Scarlett and Richarlison were on target as an under-strength Tottenham opened their pre-season tour with an entertaining 2-0 win over the A-League champions, Auckland FC, on Sunday.

Roberto De Zerbi rested most of his top players but the Premier League side dominated a match played in damp conditions. The 40,112 who packed into the All Blacks’ famed rugby ground formed the biggest crowd to watch a men’s football match in New Zealand. It surpassed the previous best of 37,034 for a New Zealand World Cup qualifying match against Peru in 2017. They were treated to a fast-paced contest, even if both sides were missing several of their best players.

Tottenham have embarked on an aggressive summer of spending after narrowly avoiding relegation last season, when they finished 17th. However, the only notable new signing to take the field was the former West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes, who scored in the 1-0 win over MK Dons in London on Wednesday.

De Zerbi said he would ease others into the tour, with Tottenham to play games in Sydney next week against the A-League side Sydney FC and their London rivals Chelsea.

“It’s a chance for the young players,” De Zerbi told TVNZ before kick-off, declaring Jan Paul van Hecke, signed from Brighton, and the former Liverpool stalwart Andy Robertson not yet up to speed. “After a very long trip, we can’t take a risk with the players who are not ready to play yet.”

The cecord club signing, Sandro Tonali, was not considered because the former Newcastle midfielder had suffered an unspecified injury – “one small problem” – before the team left London, De Zerbi added.

Fernandes came on with half an hour remaining and Spurs bagged their second goal shortly afterwards through the work of two other substitutes. Mathys Tel burst into the box and set up a tap-in for Richarlison.

Scarlett, one of several Spurs academy players in action, opened the scoring in the 12th minute, pouncing after the Auckland goalkeeper Michael Woud parried Manor Solomon’s shot.

Sports.title: Arsenal make shock approach to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal are exploring a shock deal to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid. Arsenal have inquired about the Brazil international, who has one year remaining on his contract at the Bernabéu.

It is believed any move for Vinícius – who scored 22 goals for Real last season and four for Brazil at the World Cup – is at a formative stage as Mikel Arteta seeks a marquee signing to build on the club’s first Premier League title in more than two decades.

The 26-year-old Vinícius fits that bill, with Atlético Madrid’s Julián Álvarez, RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain also on their radar.

Arsenal bolstered their attacking options with the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge this week. Morgan Rogers had also been identified as a target, but it is believed Arsenal were not prepared to pay more than £80m for the England international, who has joined Chelsea in a £117m deal – a British record fee.

Vinícius’s future at Real is uncertain after José Mourinho’s return and the club could cash in on the player, rather than risk losing him for nothing in a year’s time.

Mourinho, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabéu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinícius accused Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February. Mourinho, Benfica manager at the time, said “something happens, always” in matches where Vinícius plays. Prestianni was banned for six matches after he admitted to using homophobic language towards Vinicius.

Tzolis followed Piero Hincapié – who turned his temporary deal into a full-time switch – and the goalkeeper Illan Meslier, who was out of contract at Leeds, as Arsenal’s third addition.

Bruno Guimarães could also move to the Emirates with Arsenal keen on signing the Brazil international. After Newcastle’s 1-1 pre-season draw at Gateshead on Saturday, Eddie Howe said: “We don’t want to lose our best players. I’ve spoken to him [Guimarães] as I would do. Bruno is just a fantastic person. We’ve had some really good conversations, both before the World Cup, during the World Cup and after the World Cup.

Sports.title: Japan football great ‘King Kazu’ Miura, 59, scores first competitive goal in four years
Sports.content:
The Japanese football legend Kazuyoshi Miura scored his first competitive goal ⁠in nearly four years on Saturday, finding the net at the age of ⁠59 as ⁠Fukushima ​United thrashed Iwaki Furukawa 7-0 to advance in the Emperor’s Cup.

Miura, affectionately known ⁠as King Kazu, struck in the 52nd minute to put Fukushima 5-0 ahead, capping a trademark ⁠run into the box by meeting a teammate’s ​cutback with a first-time ‌finish at 59 ‌years and 149 days.

The goal sparked celebrations among teammates ‌on the pitch and the bench before the veteran forward was substituted three minutes later.

It was Miura’s first competitive goal since November 2022, when he scored for Suzuka PG, now Atletico Suzuka, in ‌a Japan Football League defeat by FC Osaka.

The former Japan international is preparing for ​a remarkable 42nd season as a professional after extending his loan spell with third-tier Fukushima United until June 2027.

Miura joined the club from Yokohama FC in ⁠December and will remain with Fukushima after making six ​appearances ​during a shortened 2026 ​campaign.

With Japan’s professional leagues set to switch ​from a ‌spring-to-autumn schedule to ​an ​autumn-to-spring calendar, Miura will enter his 60s next February still playing professionally, adding another chapter to one of football’s most enduring careers.

Sports.title: Defoe’s shock Woking exit came after ‘growing concerns’, says club
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe’s departure from Woking came after “growing concerns” at the club with Jody Brown, the National League side’s director of football, claiming the former Tottenham striker failed to turn up for training.

Defoe’s contract at the National League club was mutually terminated on Thursday after four months in charge. In is first managerial job, the 43-year-old oversaw two wins and one defeat in six matches. The former England forward had said it was “impossible for me to continue” and described his time at the club as an “eye-opening” experience.

But the club responded strongly on Saturday. “The recommendation to appoint Jermain as manager was mine, and I take full responsibility for it,” Brown said. “After meeting with him on several occasions, I believed he was the right person to lead the club into an exciting new era.”

But he went on: “However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns.

“To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul [Bracewell, the assistant manager] for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season. That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.

“A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and head of operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session. Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.”



Defoe has not publicly responded to Woking’s claims.

Sports.title: How Leicester City are still chasing a specialist No 9 to kickstart promotion bid... after failing to land Danny Ings and Jamie Vardy return off the cards
Sports.content:
How Leicester City are still chasing a specialist No 9 to kickstart promotion bid... after failing to land Danny Ings and Jamie Vardy return off the cards

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leicester City are clear favourites to gain promotion from League One but are still to sign a striker with barely three weeks to go until they kick-off the season against Notts County.

Manager Russell Martin may have overseen a 3-3 draw against La Liga side Malaga in Marbella on Saturday but that didn't mask what he thought the former Premier League champions were missing.

'The topline, both wide positions and a No 9, I think it’s really clear,' said the Foxes' boss when asked about priorities.

They have tried and failed to agree terms with former West Ham striker Danny Ings and, despite his appearance at first team testing, Jamie Vardy is not planning a return. He still has aspirations to finish at the top.

The scramble is on to find a proverbial horse for the course. Yet League One had an extremely rich seam of forwards to mine from last season and competition is fierce.

Manager Russell Martin has identified the key area he needs to fill for Leicester to make good on their tag of title favourites

Leyton Orient's Dom Ballard is one forward with League One pedigree on Leicester's radar

Leicester's initial focus fell on Plymouth's Lorent Tolaj - with 17 League One goals last season - but he wanted a Championship club. Preston North End tried but big-spending Bristol City succeeded.

The Ashton Gate side have also been courting Leyton Orient finisher Dom Ballard for two months, another on Leicester's radar, but a fee has still to be agreed. Exeter's Jayden Wareham, scorer of 19 league goals last season, is viewed as an alternative.

With time of the essence Martin knows Leicester need to be decisive and soon.

Aribim Pepple, the other half of Plymouth's prolific strike partnership last season, is another who has piqued the interest of analysts, with justification.

Pepple, who just missed out on making Canada's World Cup squad, had the second highest goals per minute ratio last season. One goal every 135 minutes; 16 goals in 35 league games. Wolves are among those looking to pounce there.

As concerns rise among supporters that the club is once again leaving it too late to do the crucial part of their summer trading, Martin countered: 'I'm hopeful we can get what we want before the season begins. We have a clear idea on the list we have and it's important to find the right character.'

Being runaway favourites to win League One will mean little to many of those supporters. Last summer they were eyeing a return to the Premier League. They ended with relegation to the third tier - though a six-point deduction was crucial given they finished five points off safety.

It's been a tumultuous 10-year ride since that Premier League title. Pivotal now is finding that Fox in the box to ensure they find that path back to the top.

Sports.title: Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France
Sports.content:
Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A female referee reportedly suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee in a men's friendly match in France.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay had taken charge of the friendly between Ligue 2 French side Metz and their Dutch opponents Fortuna Sittard on Sunday.

Demoncay had blown for a free kick to Fortuna Sittard in the 39th minute, after a Metz player had pulled the shirt of a breaking attacker.

The fouled Fortuna Sittard player was then seen squaring up to two Metz players following the incident.

This led to Demoncay racing over in an attempt to break up the incident, while players from both teams also ran in as the melee grew.

Footage showed Demoncay, 26, being knocked over backwards as more players pushed into the melee.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee between players during a friendly in France

Demoncay had attempted to intervene in the brawl but was knocked down as more players got involved

One player was seen signalling for medical attention with Demoncay appearing to have hit her head on the ground after falling

While unclear on the footage, Demoncay appeared to hit her head on the ground after falling.

One Fortuna player was quick to notice the stricken referee, as they stood by the official and motioned for medical staff to come to her aid.

Medical staff, assistant referees and security came onto the pitch, with Demoncay receiving assistance.

The footage showed Demoncay sitting up as medical staff began to assess her, while players appeared to have become concerned by the incident.

Demoncay was ultimately unable to continue the match, with one of her assistants forced to step in.

The incident, which played out with a sign in the background reading 'respect the referee', led to two players being booked.

Fortuna Sittard had described it as a 'remarkable moment' on the club's website.

Metz, who had been leading 1-0 at the time, went on to win 3-1 in the friendly.

Sports.title: Lucky Lando Norris WINS the Hungarian Grand Prix after team-mate Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation - while Kimi Antonelli gains the upper hand on title rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell
Sports.content:
Lucky, lucky, Lando. Not that world champion Norris was other than the fastest man in the Hungarian Grand Prix and should have won it on his own.

But he was helped, first, by a bizarre incident befalling his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri handing him the victory chance his pole position deserved and his poor first lap did not.

This first of two pivotal moments in Norris’s triumph came on lap 38 when Piastri, who had pitted for a second time, was trying to make progress back to the front. In front of him, Williams’ Carlos Sainz – the villain of the piece – was fighting with Fernando Alonso for 15th.

Distracted by this, Sainz was oblivious of Piastri behind him. It was a blue-flag time. The Spaniard should have made way. He did not. Piastri fumed: ‘Get out of the f***ing way. You idiot.’ They banged tyres. ‘Oh, my God!’

All this was delaying Piastri, obviously, while Norris was making hay out on his own. After Norris was called in at the end of the following lap, he emerged in front of the other papaya car. Job done.

Piastri was furious. Obviously with Sainz. But also, it seemed, with his McLaren team for granting Norris freedom to open up an advantage for seven laps after his own stop.

Lando Norris returned to the top step of the podium with a dominant win in Hungary

The British driver was stunned by team-mate Oscar Piastri but wrestled back control

Piastri’s race engineer Tom Stallard came on the radio, to pacify him, saying: ‘Oscar, it’s Sainz that cost us. Target is to get to the end on this tyre.’

Piastri rejoined: ‘Oh, mate, just don’t talk to me now.

‘Nice of you guys to factor that one (the traffic) in by the way, thanks.’

If he believes the team pull for Norris, their hand-reared champion, this state of affairs will hardly have put his mind to rest.

The second and final piece of luck working for Norris came as Piastri, who looked set to finish second, conked out with a gearbox problem, his race over on lap 56 of 70. Thus, without any concerns at all, Norris went on to claim the first win of his title defence, indeed since the Sao Paulo Grand Prix last November.

Now more drama ensued as a virtual safety car was enlisted. Lewis Hamilton, on a unravellingly disappointing weekend for him given what riches it promised, had succeeded the stricken Piastri in second place.

Ah, but this was not to last. Norris came in for new tyres and so did Hamilton. For Norris, fine, back out at the front. But Hamilton emerged from the pits virtually level with third-placed Kimi Antonelli, and, although the seven-time world champion pushed himself ahead of the Italian into and out of the first corner, it was not legit, given the VSC limits in place.

Was he speeding in the pits in desperation? He was placed under investigation for the offence and handed a five-second penalty a few minutes later. ‘They are handing out penalties like crazy,’ said Hamilton.

He had already been told by his pit wall to hand the place back to Antonelli, but that is not quite how it stayed: yes, Norris was first, Max Verstappen second (because he did not need to stop under the VSC, being on newer tyres than Hamilton) and Antonelli third. But Hamilton’s penalty dropped him below team-mate Charles Leclerc and into fifth place.

Norris benefitted from Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation on Sunday afternoon

Lewis Hamilton fell further back in the championship race to Kimi Antonelli

What a headache for Hamilton. Instead of clipping Antonelli’s championship lead by two points, as he was due to do prior to Piastri’s departure, he fell five points back. He is 50 behind Antonelli heading for the summer break.

Why didn’t Ferrari slow Leclerc down? Do the fools want to win the title?

George Russell, seventh on the day, is now 59 adrift, nine points down on his starting position. Not great for the Briton, but not the worst outcome given how he watched the field fly by him at the start as anti-stall kicked in on his Mercedes. He had gone down to 19th at the end of lap one, but, helped by a new engine fitted between qualifying and the race, came through the midfield.

There was little overtaking on display, though Verstappen made a brilliant pass on Hamilton at the first corner – named after his (Verstappen’s) de facto father-in-law Nelson Piquet. He caught the Briton by surprise, a typical Max mugging. It was the move of the day.

Piastri did not need to exert such virtuosity as an old Norris habit came to haunt him, his weakness on first laps that has repeatedly cost him race wins from promising starting positions, especially in 2024 when he had an outside chance of claiming the title.

He was very smartly away from pole and took the first corner in command. But he drifted wide at the second corner, named after Hamilton, and that allowed Piastri to assume the lead.

Norris seemed to have more pace than his team-mate and harried him, but Piastri held track position until his afternoon unravelled. Norris finally streaked away, finishing 15 seconds up the road and out of sight.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami teammate suffers horrifying head injury before leaving the field in an ambulance and being rushed to hospital
Sports.content:
An Inter Miami forward needed to be rushed to the hospital after a disturbing aerial collision caused him to lose consciousness and begin seizing on the pitch.

German Berterame is recovering in the hospital after taking contact to his head in a Saturday night game against CF Montreal.

In the 70th minute at the Saputo Stadium in Canada, Berterame collided with Montreal defender Efrain Morales - who made the contact from behind the player as they both jumped for a header - and landed awkwardly on the pitch.

Broadcast cameras caught an open-eyed Berterame convulsing on the ground after training staff rushed over to attend to him.

The match was stopped for ten minutes as Berterame was taken off the field on a stretcher, never appearing to re-gain consciousness.

He was eventually placed into an ambulance and was rushed to a nearby hospital.

Inter Miami's German Berterame was knocked unconscious after a collision against Montreal

Berterame needed to be transported to the hospital, where he has been recovering

Miami was awarded a penalty that was scored by Luis Suarez, who held up Berterame's shirt

After the match, Inter Miami manager Guillermo Hoyos said his striker was 'recovering right now,' adding, 'He's fine, conscious.'

'His family is aware of everything,' Hoyos said. 'They're calm. The most important thing is that he's OK, and right now he is OK.'

Due to the collision with Morales, Inter Miami was awarded a penalty. Teammate Luis Suarez converted the chance, which proved to be the only goal on the night. Suarez held up Berterame's shirt in honor of the striker.

'We were alarmed at first because the blow was very strong. On the play, it’s obvious there was an elbow, which is why a penalty was awarded, he fell like dead weight,' Hoyos recalled.

'I think he might have already been unconscious given the severity of the impact. He took that elbow and hit the ground hard.

'It was a moment of great desperation and deep sadness, because it went beyond football, and all that. It’s about human life, that’s what matters most. So, we just hope everything turns out well.'

Berterame, the Mexico international, has bagged seven MLS goals for The Herons since moving from Monterrey in January.

With the victory, Miami now sit just two points behind league-leaders Nashville SC. They next face the Columbus Crew.

Sports.title: 'F*** you and them': Jermaine Jenas hits back at his critics in bizarre pancake video after former BBC star's car-crash Good Morning Britain interview
Sports.content:
Jermaine Jenas has unequivocally hit back at his critics in bizarre fashion after uploading a topless video of himself dancing in his kitchen.

Former England and Spurs star Jenas, 43, was one of the BBC's rising stars before he was axed from his role on Match of the Day in August 2024 following the discovery of inappropriate messages sent to two women.

Jenas had served as a regular presenter on The One Show and 5Live before his wife, Ellie Penfold, confirmed she had split from the former footballer in the wake of the scandal - having been together for 16 years.

He is now in a relationship with Parisien estate agent Anne Leplaideur, 31, with the pair spotted holidaying together this summer.

He spoke at length about how he had 'lost everything' during his 'tough two-year period' in a car-crash appearance on ITV's Good Morning Britain last month, in which he was grilled by presenters Kate Garraway and Ranvir Singh.

Jenas took issue with Singh's 'line of questioning' and later claimed the presenters had 'a thirst for blood', with the former footballer accused of 'skirting around the issue' of his behaviour and responding to questions in a defensive manner.

Jermaine Jenas has hit back at his critics in a defiant Instagram message on Saturday

But taking to Instagram on Saturday, Jenas posted a defiant message while dancing and spinning a plate of white chocolate pancakes.

'I no longer care how the story gets told,' the caption read. 'F*** you and them… Respectfully.'

Rio Ferdinand responded to the post by saying: 'Okaaaaay… these tunes don't fit the caption ffs.'

The ITV interview saw Garraway ask Jenas what he had 'learned'. Jenas replied: 'To say I was happy in the industry I was in is an overstatement. When it comes to what I've learnt, it's a very specific thing to put my finger on.

'It's probably a little bit of an unfair question to find that one thing. You go through life, you make mistakes and there were things happening on the outside of work also affecting my behaviour.'

Singh then accused him of 'skirting around what you've learnt', but Jenas responded: 'I'm not skirting around anything, Ranvir.

'I'm more than happy to have the conversation, which is why I'm here. I'm not here to be defending myself in any way, shape or form.

The 43-year-old ex-footballer was grilled during a car-crash interview on GMB last month

He was accused of 'skirting around the issue' of his BBC sacking in August 2024

'I know what I did was wrong and I accept those punishments. Nobody is skirting around the responsibility of what I did. I know what I did and I know what I did was wrong. So I don't understand where that line of questioning is coming from.'

Singh then asked him for his 'advice to other men who are in positions of power in any industry and who think they are just flirting with women at work who… what is your advice to other people then who might be learning from your mistakes?'

Jenas replied: 'I think they can look at what happened to me and make their own assumptions about what they have to do with their own lives.

'I'm not here to preach to other people about what they should do with their lives. I'm here to explain to people my own experiences of what I've been through and what I've done and the impact that it's had on everybody in my life.

'I'm not here to dictate to people in terms of what they want to do. I understand why you have to come at me with this line of questioning and it's completely fine and if you feel like I have not been punished enough then go ahead and keep going.'

Singh said she was 'not saying that', adding that Jenas had spoken about 'what's been taken away from me' – but 'people might say you put yourself in that position, you risked it all by doing what you did'.

Jenas replied: 'Oh, 100 per cent. I did put myself in that position and I'm not sat here begging and pleading for my job back.

'I'm fully accepting of what has been taken away from me. I put myself in that position and that's where the learning comes from – and that's where I have to now look forward to what is coming next. That's where the post comes from.

Jenas, 43, split from wife Ellie Penfold after inappropriate messages sent to two women were discovered

'It's impossible to not learn about yourself when you are put into the position that I was put into, that I put myself into. You have to take stock, look around yourself, look at your own behaviour and realise that things have to change.

'I've done that over a period of time where it's been very tricky – granted I put myself in that position.'

Jenas deflected throughout his ten-minute interview, pleading for forgiveness because everyone 'makes mistakes'.

The 43-year-old learnt of his sacking from the BBC while live on radio.

He added: 'The learning from it doesn't always have to be negative. We are so obsessed in this industry with "oh, he's been cancelled" – everything has to be negative.

'Hang on a minute, I'm a person who has learnt a lot from my mistakes and spent ten to 12 years in this industry and had a brilliant career and really enjoyed my time on television. There's a lot for me to give back.

'I'm not saying on television, it could be on any different platform where I know a lot of people feel how I feel.

'I'm a human being. We make mistakes. You two [Singh and Garraway] can't sit in front of me and say you've never made a mistake in your life. We all make mistakes, we live in the public eye.

'Every mistake I made was made public and I had to handle that as a man. That's exactly what I did. The thing now is about moving forward and what I'm about to do next. Currently, I'm not sure.'

Sports.title: LeBron James handed major boost after 76ers move as two-time NBA champion reunites with star in Philadelphia
Sports.content:
LeBron James handed major boost after 76ers move as two-time NBA champion reunites with star in Philadelphia

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

LeBron James has received a major boost in his quest to bring a championship to Philadelphia, with two-time NBA champion Kentavious Caldwell-Pope preparing to join him with the 76ers.

Caldwell-Pope agreed to a contract buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies and plans to sign a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the 76ers after clearing waivers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

The move reunites James with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate, with whom he previously won the 2020 NBA championship inside the Orlando bubble.

The veteran star brings elite capabilities to a transformed Philadelphia roster, providing elite perimeter defense alongside proven championship experience.

Caldwell-Pope earned his second championship ring in 2023 as a starter for the Nuggets, proving his status as one of the league's most reliable shooting guards.

His arrival bolsters a loaded 76ers squad that has undergone a dramatic offseason overhaul to build an immediate title contender around Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

LeBron James has received a major boost in his quest to bring a championship to Philadelphia

Two-time NBA champion Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is preparing to join James with the 76ers

The acquisition comes just days after James stunned the basketball world by taking a historic pay cut, signing a two-year, $8 million veteran deal to join Philadelphia.

By accepting a salary below market value, James allowed the 76ers' front office flexibility to construct a championship-caliber supporting cast around their new core.

Caldwell-Pope's addition addresses a critical need on the wing, providing head coach Nick Nurse with an experienced lockdown defender capable of spacing the floor for Embiid and James.

With James, Embiid, Maxey, Jaylen Brown and now Caldwell-Pope in the fold, Philadelphia has firmly positioned itself as a favorite in the Eastern Conference.

As training camp approaches, the 76ers' aggressive summer spending spree signals a clear, all-in mandate to deliver the franchise's first NBA title since 1983.

Shortly after James' move to Philadelphia was confirmed, President Donald Trump launched an astonishing attack on the NBA legend.

On Friday, Trump was asked to weigh in on who holds the title of the greatest basketball player of all time.

'Michael Jordan's a guy that's a friend of mine, I've played golf with him,' Trump said.

The news comes days after James stunned the basketball world by taking a historic pay cut

The move reunites James with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate, with whom he previously won the 2020 NBA championship

'He's a really good guy and I think LeBron is - maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump, I don't know - but I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way.'

The comments mark the latest chapter in a long-standing feud between the four-time NBA champion and Trump, which dates back to James labeling him a 'bum' in 2017.

James, 41, has frequently used his platform to criticize Trump, previously endorsing Democratic candidates and launching voting-rights initiatives across the country.

Their bad blood spilled into the public eye during Trump's first presidency after he withdrew a White House invitation extended to Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry over his hesitation to visit.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or hopes are OVER claims Arsenal legend after star 'disappeared' in England's World Cup semi-final
Sports.content:
Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or hopes are OVER claims Arsenal legend after star 'disappeared' in England's World Cup semi-final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harry Kane's hopes of winning the Ballon d'Or are over after failing to have a major influence in England's World Cup semi-final against Argentina, according to Emmanuel Petit.

England were beaten 2-1 by Argentina in the semi-final earlier this month, with Thomas Tuchel's side stung by two late goals after Anthony Gordon had put them ahead.

Tuchel's defensive substitutions were scrutinised post-match with England having dropped deep into their own half, with the view the Three Lions had invited Argentina to keep attacking.

England captain Kane was among those to have dropped back as the match went on, with the forward unable to make an impact in Argentina's half.

Petit, who won the World Cup with France in 1998, has claimed Kane's lack of impact in the match will hold him back when it comes to voting for the Ballon d'Or.

Kane has been seen among the favourites to win the honour, which would make him the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the honour, having scored 72 goals for Bayern Munich and England during the season.

Harry Kane's chances of winning the Ballon d'Or are claimed to have taken a blow

Emmanuel Petit believes Kane's chances 'are over' after accussing him of disappearing in England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina

'Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or chances are over. If you base that only on the German league, okay, no problem at all,' Petit told Mr Gamble, via Goal.

'But in the Champions League and with the national team, when it started to be really hard to win, I think he disappeared.

'I can't point the finger at him because he tried everything he could, and he scored many goals, but he didn't have an impact in the big games, just like in the Champions League.

'I think there are a few names ahead of him.'

Kane still finished the World Cup with six goals, while he scored 14 goals in 13 games in the Champions League.

This included scoring in both legs of the quarter-finals and semi-finals against Real Madrid and PSG, respectively.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Petit has instead suggested Rodri and Lamine Yamal's performances at the World Cup will help put them in contention for the prize.

Rodri was named as the World Cup's player of the tournament, with the midfielder a crucial figure in Spain's triumph.

Petit highlighted Rodri as a leading contender after his crucial role in Spain's World Cup triumph

'Yamal, he had a great World Cup,' Petit said.

'You know the rules for the Ballon d'Or have changed so much, just like the rules on the pitch. Rodri has been the best player again during this competition. Messi had a great competition, but he plays for [Inter] Miami.

'I know the World Cup is above any title you want with your club. But in the meantime, you have to win the title. Is it going to be a Spanish player? I have no idea.

'But it's going to be tough and in the end, I hope it won't be a commercial decision.'

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update

Arsenal want Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior and are exploring a move for the Brazil international, but have already agreed to sign another player this summer

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are adding another player to their academy (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Cardiff City's youngest-ever player, Axel Donczew, is set to sign for Arsenal next week.

‌



The Gunners have agreed a deal for the Wales under-19 international, who Fabrizio Romano claims has already had a medical.

‌



Donczew, 16, debuted for the Bluebirds as a second-half substitute during their EFL Trophy match against Newport County in October, aged 15 years and 234 days. He broke a record that his team-mate Rob Tankiewicz set barely an hour earlier by starting the group stage game.

‌



Aaron Ramsey had previously held the record for 18 years. He was also the last player Arsenal signed from Cardiff.

The Gunners spent £7million on a 17-year-old Ramsey in 2018. That move came after the midfielder made 22 appearances across all competitions for Cardiff, whereas Donczew has played just twice.

The Telegraph initially reported that the Gunners were keen on the teenager, who is expected to join their academy.

‌



News of the deal surfaced less than 24 hours after Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior emerged. Real Madrid's winger would likely cost a record-breaking fee for the Gunners to sign, but they are believed to be exploring the possibility.

Jose Mourinho is reportedly reluctant to lose the Brazilian, but his lack of a new contract at the Bernabeu means Real could cash in this summer.

In terms of Donczew, he has been missing from Cardiff City's pre-season activities this summer following interest from Premier League sides. Fulham had previously expressed interest in the right-footed left winger, who can also play centrally as an attacking midfielder.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City's former Elite Development Sqyad head coach Brian Barry-Murphy believes Axel Donczew is a brilliant player (Image: Ryan Hiscott, Getty Images)

Donczew last played for Cardiff in December, making another substitute appearance during an EFL Trophy round of 32 tie against Wimbledon. A fortnight later, Donczew was included in the matchday squad for their EFL Cup quarter-final against Chelsea, but did not feature.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy said late last year: "I think if they're good enough, and he clearly is, then they're old enough for us with Axel. The former Manchester City youth coach hailed Donczew as a "brilliant player".

‌



He has already earned recognition as a Wales under-19 international. Donczew has represented his national side since the under-15s.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The youngster has racking up 11 appearances across various age groups, and also holds eligibility to feature for Poland. Wales senior side head coach Craig Bellamy, however, is said to be an admirer of the youngster.

‌



Under-21s coach Darren Purse told WalesOnline: "I think Axel came into fruition because I think Craig Bellamy really liked him as an Under-16 playing for Wales. I think that came through him and the gaffer's (Barry-Murphy) conversations."

CAA (Creative Artists Agency) Stellar represents Donczew. The prominent agency's lengthy list of clients also notably includes two current Arsenal academy players: Angelinou Pedro and Theo Julienne.

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad

Liverpool saw off Sunderland in a pre-season friendly on Saturday but they did so without Jeremy Jacquet as the summer signing was left out of the squad

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet was left out of Liverpool's squad at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Jeremy Jacquet's long-term injury led to him being left out of Liverpool's squad on Saturday with the Reds prepared to "take it easy with him".

‌



The French defender was signed in January for £55million from Rennes, but allowed to play out the season with the Ligue 1 club. He's since made the move to Anfield but did so off the back of a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

‌



The 21-year-old was forced to miss the final few months of last season after picking up a shoulder injury. Given that he have surgery on the issue, his last game came all the way back on February 7.

‌



As a result Liverpool are taking a cautious approach to bringing him back into the fold and he was left out of the team that beat Sunderland 4-2 in Nashville. Iraola explained to LFCTV: “With Jeremy, we decided to take it easy with him."

“He has been a lot of months without playing with a shoulder injury. So, I think we are going to take it easy with him. He will play probably the last game of this US tour and he will have time to have minutes. It's true that we were kind of happy but we've lost one now.”

Iraola was referring to the injury sustained by Joe Gomez, who failed to complete ten minutes during Liverpool's clash on Saturday. There is no diagnosis on his injury but the defender has been plagued by injuries for years and could further test the team's backline depth.

‌



"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe," said Iraola. "We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we've lost Joe straight away."

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet's move to Liverpool was confirmed this summer

Liverpool have seen Ibrahima Konate depart for Real Madrid after his contract expired whilst Giovanni Leoni is still getting back to 100 percent after rupturing his ACL last September. Virgil van Dijk has just turned 35 and will see his contract expire in the summer.

Article continues below

Jacquet is highly rated and was tipped to move to Chelsea, who had chased him throughout January, before Liverpool swooped in to complete a deal. He's relatively inexperienced but is likely to play a big role with Liverpool's resources already being tested in pre-season.

Sports.title: F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges
Sports.content:
F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges

F1 round-up ahead of the Hungarian Grand after Lewis Hamilton leaves one of his rivals furious

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton will line up fifth for the Hungarian Grand Prix after receiving another penalty (Image: Formula 1 via Getty Images)

A thrilling Hungarian Grand Prix is on the cards after world champion Lando Norris took his first pole position of the season. With 2026 pace-setters Mercedes struggling at the tight and twisty Hungaroring track, Ferrari went into qualifying as the favourites for pole.

‌



However, Norris took advantage of an upgraded McLaren to set the fastest time. Joining him on the front row will be Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, with the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri third and Max Verstappen of Red Bull fourth despite a spin at the end of Q3.

‌



Hungaroring specialist Lewis Hamilton had to settle for fifth after being hit with a three-place grid penalty. Mercedes' George Russell, who desperately needs a good weekend after his no-score in Belgium last weekend, lines up sixth, a place ahead of team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who was also given a grid penalty.

‌



Here's a round-up of the latest F1 news ahead of the final race before the summer break…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Fresh penalty for Hamilton

Having just missed out on pole, Hamilton suffered another blow when he was relegated three places. The seven-time world champion was deemed guilty of blocking Piastri at the first corner as the Australian started a quick lap.

‌



Ferrari failed to tell Hamilton about the oncoming McLaren and the mistake could be costly in the 41-year-old's title challenge. Hamilton has recently been no stranger to penalties. He was given a five-second penalty at the British Grand Prix for moving before the lights went out.

Lewis Hamilton one of two brutally punished as new Hungarian GP starting grid confirmed READ MORE :

In Belgium, he was controversially hit with the same sanction for his part in the first-lap clash that ended Russell's race, despite most observers viewing it as a racing incident.

Reacting to his Budapest penalty, he wrote on Instagram: "Sometimes you just can’t catch a break. Another weekend when I've been feeling great throughout all the sessions, but then it just falls apart.

‌



"To go from being so close to pole to then starting P5 is extremely frustrating. I always do my best to keep positive - sport is always about the highs and lows, but it’s also in the margins. Every point counts and you have to seize every opportunity.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"After 3 penalties in 3 weekends, it's becoming difficult to hang on to that positivity. Still, I won't let the setbacks take away from the progress we've been making as a team. With the pace we have, I'm hopeful we can get something out of the race."

‌



In a subsequent twist, Antonelli, who Hamilton trails by 45 points, was also served with a three-place grid penalty for failing to slow sufficiently under yellow flags following Verstappen's last-corner spin.

View 2 Images Oscar Piastri wasn't happy with Hamilton (Image: Getty Images)

Piastri's gesture

A previously unaired clip of Piastri's reaction to being blocked by Hamilton has emerged. The 25-year-old was impeded by the Ferrari at the start of Q3, with the Brit copping his aforementioned penalty.

Article continues below

The usually unflappable Piastri was left irate by the incident, calling it "pretty bad." In-car footage of the incident shows Piastri being clearly baulked by the Ferrari.

He then pulls up alongside Hamilton and gives him a sarcastic thumbs-up. Piastri said: "I saw him from the start line and kind of watched him, expecting him to get out of the way, and I've watched him basically all the way up until I nearly hit him."

Sports.title: Man Utd 'won't make Champions League spots' due to major concern and Bruno Fernandes factor
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'won't make Champions League spots' due to major concern and Bruno Fernandes factor

Manchester United enjoyed a stunning second half of last season but they still have their doubters as Michael Carrick looks to make an impact across an entire campaign

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is out to prove himself in his first full season at Man Utd (Image: MARKKU ULANDER, Lehtikuva/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United won't make the Champions League places next season according to Troy Deeney - who believes they'll struggle with the added amount of games.

‌



The Red Devils enjoyed a huge renaissance under Michael Carrick, who took charge in January. They had been inconsistent until his arrival before going on an impressive run, winning 12 of their final 17 games to finish third.

‌



That run came with United not in any European competition and out of both domestic cups at the first hurdle. It means, from January, they only had their Premier League assignments to focus on, which was advantageous.

‌



They will not enjoy that benefit again as Carrick looks to prove himself across a full season - and Deeney cannot see Bruno Fernandes having the same level of influence. The Portuguese playmaker won numerous individual accolades and set the record for assists.

Mason Mount opens up on new Man Utd role handed to him by Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts READ MORE :

He told talkSPORT: "I don’t think they’ll make the Champions League places right now. The reason is we don’t know what Carrick’s like with three games in a week at this level. Obviously, we saw a bit of Championship, but not at this level.

"Now, having to look at the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cups, Carabao Cups, you can’t go out as early as you have done in previous years. There’s an expectation now to do more. Bruno Fernandes, do you really think he’s going to have the season he had last season again this season?

‌



"I just think that with the squad currently constructed as is, I don’t think there’s enough depth to get through all of those competitions, which I think will ultimately leave them short."

View 2 Images Man Utd finished an impressive third last term (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

United have made it a priority to add midfielders this summer as they look to prepare themselves for next season. They built up some impressive momentum last term and have since added Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos with the middle of the pitch cited as a problem area.

Article continues below

Deeney has backed Arsenal to retain their title with Manchester City again second best. Liverpool, now under new management, are his pick for third whilst he's backed Xabi Alonso to get Chelsea back into the top four after a dire season last time out.
