World.title: Kwankwaso: Obi Will Honour His One-term Promise If Elected in 2027
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, will honour his pledge to serve only one term if elected in the 2027 presidential election.

Kwankwaso stated this during an interview on News Central’s 60 Minutes with Mr. Kay, while responding to questions about Obi’s commitment to a single four-year tenure and whether he would seek the presidency after the proposed arrangement.

According to him, Obi has publicly made the promise and should be trusted to keep his word.

“I personally believe Peter Obi is a gentleman and I have every reason to trust him, especially that he said it to the hearing of everybody. Nobody should have any reason to doubt him,” Kwankwaso said.

He explained that the power-sharing arrangement within the NDC was built on mutual trust and a collective agreement among the coalition partners.

Kwankwaso also argued that allowing the South to complete an eight-year tenure aligns with the understanding reached by members of the alliance.

“We believe the southern part of the country should complete its second term and with that, and to the hearing of everybody in this country, I don’t believe any gentleman would want to renege, would want to say no or change his or her mind,” he stated.

The former Kano State governor added that beyond individual ambitions, the coalition had developed a shared roadmap for governance that would guide whoever eventually leads the country.

According to him, the NDC’s focus is on implementing its agreed agenda rather than advancing the interests of any particular political bloc.

“More importantly, we have collectively gotten a short-term, medium-term and, of course, long-term plan for this country. It does not matter whether it is him from the Obidient side, or my humble self from the Kwankwasiyya side or another side, we believe we have an agenda,” he said.

Kwankwaso stressed that the coalition would work to ensure continuity of its programmes regardless of who occupies the presidency in the future.

“That agenda, we will as much as possible ensure that whoever comes, maybe Peter, maybe me or any other person, would stick to that programme,” he added.

World.title: Tinubu: We Will Soon Overcome Insecurity Challenges in the North
World.content:
*North has stagnated due to loss of values, says Ango Abdullahi

*Sultan seeks repentance of perpetrators of evil in Nigeria

Deji Elumoye in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna

President Bola Tinubu has said that the security challenges confronting Nigeria, particularly the northern region, will soon be overcome.

He said that his administration had put in place decisive measures to end the activities of criminal groups across the country.

This is just as the Chairman of the Northern Elders Forum (NEF) and former Vice-Chancellor of Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Prof. Ango Abdullahi, yesterday lamented the erosion of the values and leadership ideals that once defined Northern Nigeria.

He warned that the region’s worsening insecurity, poverty and underdevelopment stemmed from a departure from the principles of its founding leaders.



Meanwhile, the Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar, yesterday sought divine intervention for the true repentance of those perpetrating evil in the country.

The president made the remarks yesterday during the Third General Hassan Usman Katsina Memorial Lecture held at Arewa House, Kaduna, with the theme, “From Sacrifice to Strategy: Rekindling Gen. Hassan Usman Katsina’s Vision for a Prosperous Northern Nigeria.”

Tinubu, who was represented by his Special Adviser on Political and Other Matters, Ibrahim Masari, paid tribute to the late General Katsina, describing him as a symbol of humility, discipline, patriotism and selfless service.



He said the former military governor of the defunct Northern Region and later Chief of Army Staff played a significant role in promoting national unity and strengthening Nigeria during critical periods of its history.

According to the president, General Katsina’s commitment to the country’s unity helped lay the foundation for the democracy and freedoms Nigerians enjoy today.



Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to securing the nation and preserving the legacies of past national heroes.

“While we continue to work day and night to secure our nation, by the grace of Allah, the challenges of insecurity confronting us, particularly in Northern Nigeria, will soon be behind us,” he said.

The president also outlined several initiatives undertaken by his administration to improve education, infrastructure, transportation and energy in the North and other parts of the country.



Meanwhile, Prof. Abdullahi and a political economist, Dr. Usman Bugaje, also spoke at the occasion.

Abdullahi said the North, once admired for its discipline, integrity and sense of purpose, had lost the moral values that made it a respected region.



“The North has lost its values. You may not want to hear this, but that is the case today. If we have not lost the values we inherited from our parents and our pioneer leaders, the North will not be where it is today,” he said.

According to him, although many Northern cities have expanded physically, the virtues of honesty, sacrifice, patriotism and selfless leadership that shaped the region’s early leaders have steadily declined.



“The North is in a pathetic situation. For me, that is the only reason why the North has stagnated. Don’t worry about the buildings you see. The basic issue concerning where the North finds itself today is the loss of our values,” Abdullahi stated.

He urged Northerners to emulate the legacy of the late Gen. Katsina, describing him as one of a generation of leaders who embodied integrity, accountability and dedication to public service.



“If we can go back to those values, particularly by remembering those who inherited them and practised them, there is no doubt in my mind that the North would have been different today,” he added.

Delivering the keynote address, Bugaje said Northern Nigeria had suffered decades of economic decline, insecurity and institutional decay because it had drifted away from the visionary leadership exemplified by Hassan Katsina and his contemporaries.

“The troubles of the North are many and varied. Food production is going down daily, hundreds of thousands are being displaced from their homes, the economy has been shrinking, poverty has nearly tripled, education and healthcare have collapsed, and our human capital has been depleted,” he said.



He added that insecurity had continued to undermine agriculture, commerce and livelihoods across the region.

“It is indeed time to ask how much of the North still remains. Or, better still, how much of the sanity of the elite, especially those in government, still remains? Today, who is there to go to? Where are the General Hassans to complain to? Where exactly is the leadership? Where is the direction?” he asked.



Bugaje criticised sections of the Northern elite for merely lamenting the region’s challenges without providing practical solutions.

“It has become the pastime of the elite to sit in the comfort of their homes and say that the North is in trouble. Some even scream that the North is finished. These comments only betray the complacency, or even the complicity, of the Northern elite,” he said.

Sultan Seeks Repentance of Perpetrators of Evil in Nigeria

In a related development, the Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Sa’ad Abubakar, has sought divine intervention for the true repentance of those perpetrating evil in the country.

Speaking while playing host to the wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, in his palace in Sokoto, the monarch declared that leaders should continue to seek divine intervention, especially for those groups of people who have been perpetrating evil in the land.

According to him, his prayer was that the evildoers would come to true repentance and live appropriately.

The Sultan commended the First Lady for her various interventions through the Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI), which has touched the lives of millions of Nigerians.

First Lady Hails Monarch for His support of Tinubu’s Govt

On her part, Mrs. Tinubu expressed appreciation to the Sultan for his continued support and constant guidance to the administration of President Bola Tinubu since inception.

The First Lady who went nostalgic about the long years of relationship between the two families noted that the Sultan is always pointing the administration in the right direction.

Mrs. Tinubu explained that the purpose of her visit was to thank the Sultan.

Earlier, the state Governor, Ahmad Aliyu, thanked the First Lady for the visit to the revered monarch, reechoing the impact of the RHI in the lives of Nigerians.

World.title: In Line With Tax Reform Acts, Oyedele Inaugurates Committee to Develop 2026 VAT Modification Order
World.content:
*Says new order to provide certainty for businesses, investors, tax administrators

Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The federal government has inaugurated an Inter-Ministerial Committee to develop the 2026 Value Added Tax (VAT) Modification Order, a major step towards ensuring the smooth implementation of Nigeria’s new tax laws and providing greater certainty for businesses, investors and tax administrators.



Among others, the committee is saddled with the task of recommending a comprehensive schedule of VAT-exempt and zero-rated supplies, taking into account revenue implications, social impact, Nigeria’s treaty obligations, and regional integration commitments.

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, inaugurated the committee in his office, charging members to deliver a modern and practical VAT framework that reflects the intent of the Tax Reform Acts and responds to the realities of today’s economy.



He described the Tax Reform Acts, which came into effect on January 1, 2026, as the most extensive changes to Nigeria’s tax system in decades, noting that the reforms simplify tax administration, improve certainty, strengthen competitiveness, protect vulnerable Nigerians and create a stronger foundation for sustainable economic growth.

Oyedele explained that while the previous VAT Modification Order made under the repealed VAT Act had served its purpose, the new legal framework requires a fresh Order to provide clarity, update relevant schedules and support the effective implementation of the Nigeria Tax Act.



“This is not about reproducing an old document,” Oyedele said.

“It is about developing a VAT Modification Order that is clear, practical and responsive to the needs of a changing economy,” the minister added, according to a statement issued by the Head, Information and Public Relations, Federal Ministry of Finance, Efe Ovuakporie.



Oyedele stated that the new Order should remove uncertainty, make compliance easier for taxpayers, support investment decisions and provide tax administrators with clearer guidance in implementing the law.

He directed the committee to undertake a thorough review of the legal framework, administrative practices, and policy directives governing VAT administration, particularly the VAT-exempt and zero-rated provisions contained in Part IV of the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025, while identifying areas that require further clarification.



The minister also charged members to engage extensively with stakeholders across government, the organised private sector, professional bodies and other interest groups to validate classifications, address implementation concerns and ensure that the final recommendations are practical and balanced.



He further instructed the committee to recommend a comprehensive schedule of VAT-exempt and zero-rated supplies, taking into account revenue implications, social impact, Nigeria’s treaty obligations, and regional integration commitments.

In addition, the committee is expected to prepare a clear and implementable VAT Modification Order that aligns with the provisions of the Nigeria Tax Act and, where necessary, recommend amendments to the Tax Reform Acts and other enabling laws to strengthen implementation.



The minister urged members to ensure that every recommendation remains faithful to both the letter and the spirit of the new tax laws, adding that the Order should encourage industrial growth, support investment, promote exports, strengthen food security, encourage innovation and facilitate Nigeria’s energy transition without compromising the integrity of the VAT system.

He also stressed the need to reduce ambiguity in VAT administration so that taxpayers, investors, regulators and tax administrators can operate with greater confidence and certainty.

Oyedele further encouraged the committee to draw from international experience while ensuring that the final document reflects Nigeria’s unique economic realities and development priorities.

The committee has a six-week window to complete its assignment and submit a Draft VAT Modification Order, schedules of VAT-exempt and zero-rated supplies with their corresponding Harmonised System Codes, implementation notes, a stakeholder consultation report and recommendations on any legislative amendments considered necessary.

Membership of the committee comprises representatives of the Federal Ministry of Finance; the Nigeria Revenue Service; the Nigeria Customs Service; the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment; the Joint Revenue Board; the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria; the Tax Advisory Committee; and the Tax Justice and Governance Platform.

Expressing confidence in the calibre of the committee, the minister said the blend of expertise drawn from government and the private sector provides a strong foundation for producing a technically sound and practical instrument that will support the effective administration of VAT under the new tax regime.

“Nigerians cannot wait. Businesses need certainty. Investors need confidence. Government needs a VAT system that is easy to administer and supports growth. I urge you to approach this assignment with diligence, objectivity and a sense of urgency,” he said.

The committee’s work, he said, would shape the administration of one of Nigeria’s most important taxes, improve the ease of doing business, strengthen investor confidence and support the successful implementation of the federal government’s fiscal reform agenda.

World.title: Springboks vs All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry: ALL the fixtures
World.content:
South African rugby fans are counting down to one of the biggest events in recent memory as the Springboks prepare to host New Zealand. Image: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry website

South African rugby fans are counting down to one of the biggest events in the professional era as the Springboks prepare to host New Zealand in an unprecedented eight-match tour across South Africa and the United States.

Dubbed “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry”, the 2026 tour will see the All Blacks face South Africa’s four United Rugby Championship franchises before contesting a historic four-Test Freedom Cup series against the Springboks.

It marks the first revival of the traditional touring format between the two nations since the launch of the Tri-Nations in 1996.



Historic return of traditional tours

The tour follows an agreement reached between the South African Rugby Union (SARU) and New Zealand Rugby (NZR) to bring back the classic bilateral tours that defined international rugby for decades before professionalism reshaped the calendar.

Instead of meeting only during the Rugby Championship, New Zealand will spend more than a month in South Africa, recreating the touring traditions that produced some of rugby’s greatest contests.

The Rugby Championship has consequently shifted to a biennial format from 2027 onwards.

Four provinces to test the All Blacks

Before facing the Springboks, the All Blacks will tackle South Africa’s strongest provincial sides:

Friday, 7 August: Stormers vs New Zealand, Cape Town Stadium, Cape Town – 19:00

Stormers vs New Zealand, Cape Town Stadium, Cape Town – 19:00 Tuesday, 11 August: Sharks vs New Zealand, Hollywoodbets Kings Park, Durban – 19:00

Sharks vs New Zealand, Hollywoodbets Kings Park, Durban – 19:00 Saturday, 15 August: Bulls vs New Zealand, Loftus Versfeld, Pretoria – 19:00

Bulls vs New Zealand, Loftus Versfeld, Pretoria – 19:00 Tuesday, 25 August: Lions vs New Zealand, Ellis Park, Johannesburg – 19:00

The provincial fixtures are expected to provide valuable preparation for both the visitors and South Africa’s leading franchises.

Four-Test Freedom Cup series

The centrepiece of the tour will be an expanded four-match Test series between rugby’s two most successful nations.



The fixtures are:

Saturday, 22 August: First Test, Ellis Park, Johannesburg – 17:05

First Test, Ellis Park, Johannesburg – 17:05 Saturday, 29 August: Second Test, Cape Town Stadium, Cape Town – 17:05

Second Test, Cape Town Stadium, Cape Town – 17:05 Saturday, 5 September: Third Test, FNB Stadium, Johannesburg – 17:05

Third Test, FNB Stadium, Johannesburg – 17:05 Saturday, 12 September: Fourth Test, M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore, United States – TBC

The final Test will make history as the first Springbok-All Blacks encounter to be played in the United States.

Women’s curtain-raiser

Adding another historic element to the tour, the Springbok Women will face the Black Ferns in a curtain-raiser at FNB Stadium on 5 September, giving supporters a showcase of both men’s and women’s international rugby on the same day.

Springboks begin preparations

South Africa recently named a 43-player squad under head coach Rassie Erasmus ahead of their one-off warm-up clash against Argentina and the New Zealand series.

The expanded squad reflects the physical demands of a tour that will stretch over five weeks against rugby’s oldest rivals.

New Zealand are expected to name their 44-man squad on Monday, 27 July.

A rivalry unlike any other

The Springboks and All Blacks have long set the benchmark in world rugby, with their rivalry spanning more than a century.

The 2026 tour promises to reignite the tradition of extended international tours, giving supporters multiple opportunities to witness one of sport’s most celebrated rivalries while providing a unique test for both nations ahead of the next Rugby World Cup cycle.

World.title: Rassie to split Springbok squad this week
World.content:
The Springboks are next in action when they face Argentina on 8 August in a one-off clash that will serve – at least in part – as important preparation for the All Blacks’ four-Test tour in August and September.

With several Springbok stars returning from injury and in need of game-time, Erasmus is likely to take a fairly strong squad to Buenos Aires, but just as importantly other players will remain in South Africa to prepare for the All Blacks series.

That split squad system is set to be revealed this week.



““Some players are returning from injury and need some valuable game time, so depending on how they progress from their injuries during next week’s training camp, we will decide who we will take to Argentina,” Erasmus commented.

“While the other guys in the 43-man squad will remain behind in Johannesburg with a group of coaches and management to begin preparing for the Tests against New Zealand.”

Springboks won’t underestimate Argentina

Erasmus said he was wary of the challenge Argentina posed, given the fact that the teams have met annually in the Rugby Championship, while the Pumas also had competitive Nations Championship Tests against Scotland and England, and defeated Wales.



“They are a quality team, and they have proved that in our previous clashes,” said Erasmus. “In fact, they defeated us in Argentina the last time we faced them there in 2024, so we know how tough it is to win there, and we intend to take a quality team to Buenos Aires.”

Erasmus added: “We are limited in the number of players we can take to Argentina, so it makes sense to give everyone a fair chance to compete for spots in the RGR (Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry) squad, and some of the players who will train in Johannesburg will be in the final stages of their recovery from injuries, which will allow them to do so under the supervision of our medical team.

“Then there are other players who have played a lot of rugby this year and for us during the Nations Championship, and need a match off to allow their bodies to recover.”

World.title: Charlize Theron’s ‘The Odyssey’ role has South Africans heading to Ster-Kinekor
World.content:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey has delivered a major boost to South Africa's cinema industry, helping Ster-Kinekor record its strongest IMAX opening weekend in more than six years. Image: Universal

Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has delivered a major boost to South Africa’s cinema industry, helping Ster-Kinekor record its strongest IMAX opening weekend in more than six years.



The epic adaptation packed cinemas across the country, with several IMAX screenings selling out as moviegoers flocked to experience the film on the biggest screens available.

Biggest IMAX opening since before the pandemic

According to Ster-Kinekor, The Odyssey has become its best-performing IMAX opening weekend since 2019, marking one of the cinema chain’s strongest premium-format launches ever.

“For Ster-Kinekor, this is the biggest IMAX opening weekend since 2019. The Odyssey opening weekend officially ranks as one of the best-performing IMAX titles on opening weekend in Ster-Kinekor’s history,” said Lynne Wylie, Chief Marketing Officer at Ster-Kinekor Theatres.

The film’s stacked cast, which includes South Africa’s Charlize Theron, was always certain to draw huge numbers to cinemas, including:

Matt Damon as Odysseus

Tom Holland as Telemachus

Anne Hathaway as Penelope

Robert Pattinson as Antinous

Lupita Nyong’o as Helen of Troy

Zendaya as Athena

Charlize Theron as Calypso

Elliot Page as Sinon

Jon Bernthal as Menelaus

The last films to generate similar IMAX demand were blockbuster releases including:

Avengers: Infinity War (2018)

Avengers: Endgame (2019)

The Lion King (2019)

Global box office success

The South African success reflects the film’s strong international performance.



According to Exhibitor Relations, The Odyssey grossed $263.5 million worldwide during its opening weekend, surpassing its reported $250 million production budget in just three days.

The impressive debut has cemented the latest Christopher Nolan film as one of the biggest box office successes of the year.

Streaming competition fails to slow cinemas

The strong turnout also provides another positive sign for traditional cinemas, which have faced growing competition from streaming services in recent years.

Nolan has long argued that his films are designed for the theatrical experience, particularly IMAX, where audiences can fully appreciate the large-scale visuals, immersive sound and cinematic spectacle.

South African audiences appear to agree, with social media filled with praise for the film’s breathtaking cinematography, epic battle scenes and IMAX presentation.

Many viewers have encouraged others to catch the film on the biggest screen possible before its premium-format run ends.



More blockbusters on the way

Ster-Kinekor believes the momentum will continue through the remainder of the year, with several major releases still to come.

Upcoming blockbuster releases include:

Spider-Man: Brand New Day – 31 July

– 31 July Street Fighter – 16 October

– 16 October The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping – 20 November

– 20 November Dune: Chapter 3 – 18 December

– 18 December Avengers: Doomsday – 18 December

– 18 December Jumanji: Open World – 25 December

South African audiences can also look forward to Children of Blood and Bone, starring South African actress Thuso Mbedu, which is set for an IMAX release on 15 January 2027.

Filmed entirely in South Africa, the fantasy epic features an international cast including Viola Davis, Idris Elba, Chiwetel Ejiofor and Cynthia Erivo.

With The Odyssey filling cinemas and attracting audiences back to the big screen, the latest box office figures suggest there is still strong demand for blockbuster films that deliver a truly immersive theatrical experience.

World.title: ‘Unnecessary’: Gayton criticised over Jayden Adams’ funeral speech
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has been criticised over his “unnecessary” and “irrelevant” speech at the funeral service of Jayden Adams on Saturday, 26 July in Stellenbosch.

The Minister of Sport was invited to address the group of mourners, which included the late Bafana Bafana’s family and friends, soccer colleagues and SAFA and Sundowns management.

Jayden is believed to have taken his own life earlier this month, just weeks after returning from the national team from the FIFA World Cup.



GAYTON MCKENZIE SLAMMED OVER JAYDEN ADAMS SPEECH

Gayto McKenzie was one of several prominent delegates who attended the funeral of Jayden Adams

Others included SAFA President Danny Jordaan, Bafana Bafana coach Hugo Broos, and the President of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and Sundowns FC, Patrice Motsepe.

Gayton kicked off his speech by sympathising with Jayden’s loved ones. He also used the opportunity to call out social media trolls who had blamed Jayden’s partner, Aqueelah Adendorf, for his shock death.

Thereafter, the minister was accused of going off on a tangent, speaking on topics like

Complimenting Patrice Motsepe’s wife, Dr Precious Moloi-Motsepe, on her fashion sense and success. Commending Tlhopie Motsepe on being well-mannered and an astute businessman

Recalling how he once took his girlfriend to a party hosted by his pal, Kenny Kunene

Claiming that Bafana coach texted him that ‘I never used to like you’

Mocking Kaizer Chiefs for not winning a trophy for the last 2 decades

Calling out football “hooligans” who “used their R5 data to insult our players”

Unnecessary things @GaytonMcK said at Jayden Adams' funeral🤦🏾‍♂️:



• "Kaizer Chiefs haven’t won a trophy in 10 years."

• "When Kenny Kunene had his 28th birthday party, I had a new girlfriend."

• "Yaya Sithole suffered abuse after we lost to Mexico. He suffered segregation,… pic.twitter.com/28tLib6UON — Commander!!! (@maetsebane) July 26, 2026

Here’s what social media users had to say about Gayton’s speech…



@SocietyNews: “His entire speech was cringe”

@SilenceEstelle: “He should have just said condolences to the family and sat down. Less is more”

@DesireTablai: “That’s the reason why politicians must never be given the platform at a funeral to deliver a eulogy. They start speaking nonsense instead of about the person who died and the family”.

INSENSITIVE?

Gayton McKenzie was also criticised by the public after the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture posted a video of the minister looking into the casket of Jayden Adams.

In a statement a day earlier, the Adams family shared that only a select few would be permitted to view the body of the late player.

The family also prohibited the public from taking pictures or videos of the funeral for posting on social media.

World.title: Body of SA Under-18 prop Luqobo Makwedini returns home to South Africa
World.content:
The body of promising South African rugby player Luqobo "Bibo" Makwedini has returned home following his tragic death in France. Image: X @GaytonMcKenzie

The body of promising South African rugby player Luqobo “Bibo” Makwedini has returned home following his tragic death in France after collapsing during a training session with French club AS Béziers Hérault.

The 20-year-old’s body arrived in the Eastern Cape and has been taken to a funeral parlour in Quigney, KuGompo City, where it will remain while funeral arrangements are finalised.

BREAKING NEWS | The body of 20-year-old rugby player Luqobo Makwedini, who died after collapsing following a training session in France, has arrived in South Africa. pic.twitter.com/Gp1vTUXYjp  July 26, 2026

Rising star’s career cut short

Makwedini, a former South African Under-18 tighthead prop, had recently embarked on a professional career in France after signing a three-year contract with Béziers.

The former Wynberg Boys’ High School standout collapsed after a morning training session at the Stade de la Gayonne and was rushed to hospital, where he died a few hours later.

While early reports indicated he had suffered heatstroke, French media have since reported that he is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest.

The exact cause of death has not yet been officially confirmed.

A bright future ahead

Standing 1.76m tall and weighing 119kg, Makwedini was regarded as one of South Africa’s brightest young front-row prospects.

He earned SA Under-18 honours after impressing for Wynberg Boys’ High School, where he built a reputation for his powerful scrummaging and surprising mobility around the field.



After joining the Béziers academy ahead of the 2025/26 season, the talented prop had reportedly been earmarked for promotion to the senior squad for the upcoming Pro D2 campaign but never got the opportunity to make his first-team debut.

Tributes pour in

Béziers president and former Springbok captain Bob Skinstad led the tributes following the youngster’s passing.

“Luqobo joined our training center during the off-season and quickly became a valued member of the Red and Blue family,” Skinstad said.

“His commitment, kindness, and personal qualities deeply impressed everyone at the club.

“Today, the entire Red and Blue family is united in mourning and deeply shaken by this heartbreaking loss.”

The French professional rugby players’ union, Provale, supporters’ group Rugbiterre and members of the wider rugby community also paid tribute to the promising South African, while recognising the support provided to Makwedini in France by club official Saul Loggenberg.

President offers condolences

President Cyril Ramaphosa has extended his condolences to Makwedini’s family, friends and loved ones following the tragedy.

The President joined the growing chorus of tributes to a young player whose life and career were cut tragically short just as he was beginning to make his mark in professional rugby overseas.

Funeral details are expected to be announced once the family has finalised the arrangements.

World.title: Why Kaizer Chiefs and Scottland FC held a moment of silence
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs and Scottland FC paused for a moment of silence. Images via Facebook/Scottland FC/ BossoFans

Kaizer Chiefs and Scottland FC joined the football fraternity in mourning after holding a moment of silence before their Toyota Cup Challenge match at the Royal Bafokeng Stadium.

The tribute was held in honour of Highlanders Football Club chairman Kenneth Mhlophe, vice chairman Fiso Siziba and treasurer Nkani Khoza, who died in a tragic road accident in Zimbabwe on Thursday evening.

Highlanders officials killed in tragic road accident

The three Highlanders officials were killed while travelling back from Kariba, where the Bulawayo giants had suffered a 1-0 defeat against ZPC Kariba on Wednesday.



According to reports, the officials were travelling in a Ford Raptor when the vehicle struck a cow at around 8pm in Lochard, approximately 50km outside Bulawayo along the Harare-Bulawayo highway.

The vehicle later collided with a bus travelling in the opposite direction, resulting in the deaths of the three club officials.

A woman who was travelling with the Highlanders executives was thrown from the vehicle when it overturned and was subsequently hit by another car, killing her instantly.

The deaths of Mhlophe, Siziba and Khoza sent shockwaves through Zimbabwean football, with tributes pouring in from across the sporting community.

The trio were returning from Kariba after supporting Highlanders in their league fixture, with their deaths coming at a significant moment in the club’s history as it celebrates its centenary year.

The Zimbabwe Football Association (ZIFA) described the loss as “immeasurable” for Highlanders, the city of Bulawayo and Zimbabwean football as a whole.



The association said the three officials’ “unwavering commitment, selfless service and leadership made an enduring contribution to one of the country’s most iconic football institutions.”

ZIFA president Nqobile Magwizi said the football community had lost three dedicated leaders whose passion helped shape Highlanders.

“We are devastated by this heartbreaking tragedy, and our thoughts and prayers are with the families of Kenneth Mhlophe, Fiso Siziba and Nkani Khoza, as well as the entire Highlanders family,” Magwizi said.

He added that the timing of the tragedy was particularly painful as Highlanders celebrates its 100th anniversary.

“It is especially painful that this loss comes during Highlanders’ centenary year, a time that should have been filled with celebration and reflection on a remarkable legacy. Instead, the football family is united in mourning.”

Kaizer Chiefs and Scottland FC honour Highlanders trio

The moment of silence at the Royal Bafokeng Stadium before the Toyota Cup clash showed the unity of the football community across borders.

Kaizer Chiefs, Scottland FC and supporters paused to remember the Highlanders officials, whose contribution to Zimbabwean football left a lasting legacy.

The tribute highlighted the strong ties between clubs in the region, with the football fraternity coming together during a time of grief.

World.title: Jayden Adams’s partner breaks silence on rumours: ‘It’s unfair’
World.content:
Jayden Adams’s girlfriend, Aqueelah Adendorf, has broken her silence after receiving death threats and being accused of being involved in his death. This comes a day after the 25-year-old’s funeral in Stellenbosch on Saturday, 25 July.



The young woman is the mother of the late Bafana Bafana player’s five year old daughter.

Jayden – who reportedly ended his life earlier this month – also has a toddler son with another woman.

JAYDEN ADAMS’S GIRLFRIEND BREAKS SILENCE

On Sunday morning, Aqueelah Adendorf broke her silence on being blamed for Jayden Adams’s alleged suicide.

She shared in an Instagram Story: “The amount of false stories and assumptions being spread about me is heartbreaking. It’s unfair to make me the villain based on rumours. I don’t owe strangers an explanation. But I do ask for one thing; please stop spreading lies and stop using Jayden’s name to create a story”.

She added: “He deserves to be remembered with dignity and respect”

Jayden Adams’s girlfriend has broken her silence on ‘false rumours’.

Image via IG

Aqueelah’s comments came a week after a report that claimed that she had had a heated spat with Jayden Adams, after visiting a nightclub just hours before he reportedly took his life.



The publication claimed that the couple, believed to have been intoxicated, had argued about money and his friends.

RECEIVING DEATH THREATS

Speaking at Jayden Adams’s funeral, Minister of Sport Gayton McKenzie publicly defended the Bafana player’s girlfriend.

He claimed that as a result of public scrutiny, the woman had been receiving death threats.

He said: “I want to get the negativity out of the way. I saw many articles blaming Aqueelah for what has happened here today. I want to say to you, Aqueelah, People will talk”.

He added, “I spoke to Jayden, and I know how he felt about you. Let people say what they want to. You loved Jadyn and were there for him. Thank you”.

In a Facebook Live earlier this week, Gayton vowed to protect and support Jayden’s partner.



He said, “I called her and told her that I will support her. I’m dealing with those threats.

“Couples do argue, you know that. She has lost the father of her child, where’s your sensitivity?”

World.title: Inside SAPS’ R18m bust: Counterfeit condoms and illicit vodka
World.content:
Seized counterfeit and illicit goods, including bottles of illicit vodka and stock recovered from storage units in Boksburg during a SAPS operation that uncovered products worth more than R18.27 million. Image: SAPS

The South African Police Service (SAPS) has seized more than 1.5 million counterfeit and illicit items worth R18.27 million during a raid on storage units in Boksburg, east of Johannesburg.



The operation uncovered counterfeit consumer goods ranging from Trust condoms and BIC pens to Nike tracksuits, alongside thousands of bottles of illicit vodka.

SAPS raids Boksburg storage units

According to Gauteng SAPS spokesperson Captain Tintswalo Sibeko, the Gauteng Provincial Counterfeit Unit conducted the operation on Friday, 24 July, with brand protection investigators after obtaining a search and seizure warrant.

The multidisciplinary team searched four storage units in Boksburg, in the Ekurhuleni District.

Police confiscated 1 459 548 counterfeit items valued at about R18.2 million.

The seized goods included:

902 016 Trust condoms

326 400 BIC pens

156 096 Kiwi shoe polish products

44 160 Nivea roll-on deodorants

24 192 Lover Plus products

5 184 Super Black hair dye products

1 500 Nike tracksuits

Officers also seized 14 370 bottles of illicit 100ml vodka, valued at R71 850.



In total, authorities confiscated 1 531 398 items with a combined estimated value of R18 271 850.

SAPS warns of risks posed by counterfeit goods

Sibeko said SAPS remains committed to protecting consumers, supporting legitimate businesses and disrupting criminal networks involved in the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of counterfeit and illicit goods.

She said these crimes damage South Africa’s economy, undermine lawful trade and expose consumers to potentially harmful products.

SAPS has urged the public and business owners to report the manufacture, storage or sale of counterfeit goods to their nearest police station or via the Crime Stop hotline on 08600 10111.

World.title: Over 72,000 foreign nationals processed for repatriation – Minister Kubayi
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Border Management Authority has processed 72,906 repatriations across all ports of entry.

This is according to Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi.

She announced the figures at an Interministerial Committee (IMC) on Migration media briefing in Pretoria.

“The Border Management Authority has processed at all its ports of entry 72,906 repatriations for the period between 7 June and 14 July,” Kubayi said.

She said government had also nabbed more than 300 foreign nationals for pending crimes.

“Law enforcement authorities have registered 354 cases of arrests and prosecutions are still pending. An additional 69 people were arrested in Jeffries Bay last weekend and appeared in court on Monday,” she said.

Kubayi urged everyone to respect the work of the authorities and abide by the law.

“We would like to issue a strong warning against those who undermine the work of our law enforcement officers or otherwise face the consequences.

“Government and social partners have been coordinating assistance to vulnerable foreign nationals affected by recent tensions and displacement.

“Government is firmly committed to implementing a migration system That is secure. Humane, lawful, and aligned with the values of our constitution.”

Two Ghanaian nationals had submitted a petition to the International Criminal Court asking it to examine years of xenophobic violence in South Africa. This petition has failed.

“We have been advised legally that this filing fails to satisfy the statutory legal triggers and jurisdictional requirements necessary for action by the court,” she added.

World.title: "Jayden was die GOAT"
World.content:
Die Mamelodi Sundowns- en Bafana Bafana-ster Jayden Adams is in sy tuisdorp, Stellenbosch, ter ruste gelê. Familie, vriende en lede van die sokkergemeenskap het by die Coetzenburg-sportterrein byeengekom om hul laaste eer aan die 25-jarige middelveldspeler te betoon.

Adams, wat liefdevol as "Grootman" bekend gestaan het, is twee weke gelede dood in 'n woonstel in Kaapstad aangetref. Hy is geloof as een van Suid-Afrika se grootste sokkertalente.

Die oorsaak van sy dood word steeds ondersoek.

World.title: ‘I am stumbling along’ –  Luqobo Makwedini’s older brother
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - The remains of South African rugby player Luqobo ‘Bibo’ Makwedini have arrived home from France.

Makwedini died earlier this month following a training session with his French club.

Sihle Makwedini, Bibo’s older brother, said the promising young player would be laid to rest on 1 August in Qumrha.

“Bibo was everything to me. As an older brother, having to also be a guardian to people, a friend, I think I've lost. It's like a pot with three feet. I've lost one and I'm stumbling along and I will miss our conversations every night. The video calls, checking up on him while he's abroad.

“Obviously it was a new environment for him as well and I had to be there to support him in terms of getting used to the environment. I'll miss everything about Bibs. From our conversations to our little chats together. I'll miss everything about him,” he said.

Eastern Cape Sport MEC Sibulele Ngongo said they are working closely with the family.

"We have been providing support for the family even during the repatriation process. While Bibo doesn't qualify for a Provincial Funeral, due to the application not being approved, we will provide support for the funeral as well."

World.title: eThekwini Mayor pleased with municipality’s financial condition
World.content:
DURBAN – Mayor Cyril Xaba said eThekwini is one of the country's best-run municipalities.

He points to the metro's ability to pay its service providers and overall financial health.

But it’s not all rosy.

Durban has been struggling with infrastructure problems, including water interruptions and sewage spills at its beaches.

“eThekwini is among the best performing municipalities in the country, particularly when it comes to financial management.

“I'm pleased to report that the independent ratings agency, GCR, has affirmed the municipality's AA negative long-term investment credit rating and A1 positive short-term rating while revising the outlook from negative to stable. Simply put, the municipality has maintained a strong financial position and experts are increasingly confident that its finances will remain stable,” Xaba said.

World.title: Former PRASA CEO unlucky as SIU targets assets
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Special Investigating Unit has secured a preservation order freezing two luxury properties linked to former PRASA CEO Lucky Montana.

The move forms part of the SIU's ongoing efforts to recover assets allegedly acquired through corruption.

Its investigation has uncovered a money trail linking the properties to PRASA's controversial R5.6 billion Integrated Security Access Management System tender.

That contract was awarded to Siyangena Technologies.

The two properties are in Hurlingham, Johannesburg, and Waterkloof, Pretoria. Combined, they are worth nearly R16 million.

The Special Tribunal has prohibited Montana from selling, transferring, leasing or otherwise dealing with the properties while the SIU's civil recovery proceedings are underway.

World.title: ‘We’re beginning to see changes’ - Joburg mayor Dada Morero
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg Mayor Dada Morero has said this year's 702 Walk the Talk is about more than just promoting an active lifestyle.

He said the event reflects growing confidence in Johannesburg's inner city, bringing together residents, businesses and government in a shared effort to reclaim and restore the CBD.

Morero said the strong turnout is an encouraging sign for a city struggling to make progress in tackling its problems and rebuilding confidence.

“It's an important part and for us it's also about reclaiming the City of Johannesburg, reclaiming our city. We are quite delighted that it's actually happening right here in the centre where we're trying to reclaim, restore the dignity, restore order within Johannesburg.

“Secondly, we're excited about the partners who constitute the Walk the Talk. Everybody, private sector, government, we've come together. Walk the Talk would not have chosen Johannesburg to come to for the walk if we still have a lot of problems.

“It's an indication that all the problems that we're faced with, we're beginning to see changes; we're beginning to see an improvement, which is a good thing and Johannesburg must continue to protect its residents.

World.title: Judge’s faith in traditional healers clashes with doctors’ prognosis
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Free State High Court Judge Lepono Lekale has put his recovery in the hands of traditional healers.

This is despite medical doctors warning that his health is expected to deteriorate further.

Judge Lekale has been absent from judicial duties for the past eight years due to serious health complications.

But he's adamant that with the help of traditional healers, his poor eyesight will be restored.

Judges Matter’s Mbekezeli Benjamin said the law provides for acceptance of sick notes from traditional healers.

“Our law in South Africa does recognise guidance, counselling, advice from traditional doctors or traditional healers as a valid basis on which, for example, to take sick leave.

“You can take sick leave and consult a traditional healer and submit a sick note from a traditional healer. It is as valid as a Western doctor. So that is, I think, where the difficulty or the conundrum was, even during his testimony at the tribunal last week.

“The tribunal panel was asking Judge Lekale, yes, the doctors are saying that your condition seems to be permanent and it does seem to be deteriorating as time goes by, but you are saying that your traditional doctors have said that you have a prospect of getting vision soon.

“So how do we reconcile the two? And he was adamant; the judge was adamant that he believes that he will get better soon. That is what his traditional doctors are saying. And he is relying on that to say that he does believe that he suffers from incapacity, but that his condition will improve. So there is that tension, and it will be up to the tribunal to look at both sides and determine what it means for the judiciary.”

World.title: Taxi licence backlog a thing of the past, says Gauteng MEC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The taxi industry has raised concerns over the slow issuing of operating licences and compliance documents.

Gauteng Roads and Transport MEC Kedibone Diale-Tlabela said the backlog in taxi operating licences has been reduced.

The department has given out more than 3,000 operating licences since November 2025. That's because of improvements in administrative and internal capacity in the department.

"We don't like law enforcement as a society, generally. We want it, we want to see it happen, but when it happens we don't want it.

“And I think this is a classical case. Remember we came in, there have been challenges, well pronounced by the industry, and we started focusing on dealing with the challenges.

“And amongst them is backlog on operating licenses, which by the way, were far advanced. Now we're issuing operating licenses to individual operators in our province.

“The backlog is gone. Now we are entering what we've been suspecting. That's a massive milestone. No, it is, it is. When you win, you win. And I think we did our best; we won because we worked closely with them, we partnered with them to understand the material contradictions.”

World.title: Dead or alive? Mystery deepens over Kenyan feared dead in Ukraine as state says he is alive
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Martin Macharia (left) and Peter Kimemia in Russia. [Courtesy]

The family of the first Kenyan that Ukraine reported killed on the Russian war front has been receiving conflicting information from the state about the matter.

The family says Martin Mburu Macharia, a former matatu driver, was killed in November 2025. His wife Grace Gathoni and children saw pictures of his body that were shared by the Ukrainian authorities. He was killed during an operation in Ukrainian territory being claimed by Russia.

However, responses from the State Department of Diaspora Affairs have, on two occasions, claimed that he is alive, ‘and in camp’ locked up on the frontline in Ukraine.

“When I went to the State Department of Diaspora Affairs in April, they told me that they did not have information about Macharia,” Gathoni told The Standard last week

“I went again at the beginning of this month (July) and officials told me that he was in the camp but has to serve his contract and finish before he is released.” she added.

Gathoni said the department has told her the same information on three different occasions

“Two different officials have given me that message. Felix told me that he is now the one handling my case,” she said.

The Standard established that Felix is an awarded Foreign Service Official at the State Department of Aiaspora Affairs who was behind the high-risk Myanmar diaspora evacuation where over 350 Kenyans were freed following regional military crackdowns, with 119 successfully repatriated last year.

He was conferred with the Order of the Grand warrior of Kenya during the 2025 Jamhuri Day celebrations.

It was not the first time for Gathoni to receive such disturbing news, early in the year while looking for answers after The Standard broke the news of the death of her husband she managed to contact a Russian national that the family knew identified as Alex. She described the man as an agent her husband had been dealing with since his recruitment into the Russian army. Alex told her that Macharia was alive but no one could reach him because he was engaged on the frontline.

“He has to serve his entire contract before we release him,” read the WhatsApp post that Gathoni received from the man. “That was in January. “

In early February Gathoni received a letter from the Russian embassy in Nairobi addressed to her lawyer Christopher Wainaina of Chacha and Company advocates. The letter acknowledged Macharia having signed a contract to join the Russian Army and described him as missing in action since December 1, 2025.

“The Embassy of the Russian Federation in the Republic of Kenya hereby communicates that the citizen of Kenya Mburu Martin Macharia, born 28/08/1987, signed the contract for serving in the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation on 25/10/2025” The letter says and adds “On 01/12/2025 he was declared missing in action.”

The letter was signed by Alexey Zamilatskiy, Head of the consular section.

In late November 2025, The Standard received pictures of the body, a copy of his passport and a boarding pass, documents that were in his possession during his short stint in the Russian army. The pictures were shared with his family which confirmed identity.

Recruited in Nairobi in October 2025, Macharia landed in Russia in late October and was reportedly coerced into signing a contract written in Russian on October 25. He came to know the details of the contract after he was shipped into a Russian military camp and told he had joined the army. He was reportedly killed on the frontline in Ukraine on November 27, 2025, 32 days after his arrival as Ukrainian troops engaged Russian frontline forces in Donetsk-Lyman, a city within the Donbass region still under Ukrainian control.

Macharia had been dispatched to the frontline despite his protestations through letters he sent to Kenya’s mission in Moscow. Copies of the letters were shared through WhatsApp to his sister Salome Macharia back at home during the rare moments that he accessed his phone and network after field operations.

He was among a team of fresh recruits from Africa in October 2025. Among the documents shared by Ukrainian authorities after his death included pictures and passports belonging to a Nigerian recruit, Stephen Udoka, who was killed alongside him. His passport, a copy of which The Standard accessed, indicated that he was 37 years old -two years younger than Macharia, who was 39.

Details shared by our sources in Kyiv's security circles included boarding passes revealing that Macharia left Nairobi aboard AirArabia on October 21, 2025, at 1350 hours en route to Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, for a connecting flight to Moscow. That was six days before The Standard, on October 27, 2025, exposed the misfortune befalling Kenyans getting duped by unscrupulous agencies operating in Nairobi promising them jobs in Russia.

Gathoni, at a meeting in mid-July with Diaspora Affairs Principal Secretary Roselyn Njogu, asked for clarity in reports about her missing husband. She told the department’s officials that Russian authorities had informed her through her lawyer that Macharia was Missing in Action a month after seeing pictures of his body.

The PS reiterated her earlier stand, which she had stated in a statement to The Standard, that her department had been seeking answers from a foreign government through diplomatic channels and will avail information whenever it comes.

The name of Macharia is also missing on a list published by Ukrainian Authorities of 485 Africans said to have been killed while fighting for Russia in the ongoing war. The over 400 are spread across Africa with Cameroon leading other African countries in losing the largest number of its sons to Russia’s war. The country has lost 104 men. Ghana takes the second position with 85 individuals. Egypt is third with 81 men killed, and Kenya lost 59.

The list is available on a new website launched by the Ukrainian Department of Defence in May, titled Stop Russian Recruiters, which documents and shares information on predatory recruitment practices of the Russian Armed Forces.

There is currently no official diplomatic communication confirming the demise of Martin Macharia, said the Diaspora Affairs department in its response to questions from The Standard. The department, however, owned up to the fact that Macharia’s family had notified it of reports of his death on the frontline.

“Consequently, the Department initiated a formal verification protocol through the Embassy of the Republic of Kenya in Moscow,” Said the letter in part adding.

“The Kenya Embassy in Moscow has since written to the Russian authorities requesting an official status update on Mr. Macharia, and is awaiting feedback”

The department promised that the family will be updated immediately upon receipt of officially verified information through the appropriate diplomatic channels.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).
