World.title: Kihnu, Vormsi ferries go on strike over pay conditions
World.content:
Strikes are going ahead Sunday lunchtime on ferries serving two of Estonia's smaller islands after no breakthrough was made on pay negotiations between union and employer.

The industrial action, known as a warning strike, affects ferries between the mainland and the islands of Kihnu and Vormsi, after 13 ferry crews and their employer failed to reach a wage agreement.

Union boss Jüri Lember told ERR the Ormsö ferry is remaining in Sviby harbor in Vormsi, between noon and 1 p.m. Sunday and so not sailing its regular route at that time to Rohuküla, on the mainland.

Similarly the Kihnu Virve will be docked at Kihnu harbor over the same time period, instead of sailing to Munalaiu.

Strikers in Sviby, on the island of Vormsi. The placards read 'We demand a fair wage for seafarers' and 'Together we are stronger'. Source: Kristi Raidla

Initially the warning strike for the Kihnu Virve had been planned for a time when it would have been in port on the mainland, later in the afternoon.

The Estonian Independent Seafarers' Union (Eesti meremeeste sõltumatu ametiühing) had turned to the national conciliator in an effort to reach a collective agreement with ferry operator Kihnu Veeteed. The union had sought a pay rise of up to 30 percent plus the indexation of wages next year.

While a response was due from Kihnu Veeteed by 2 p.m. last Wednesday, none was received, prompting the crews of the two ferries to go ahead with the strike.

The seafarers' union said it has been trying to reach a collective agreement with the employer since March 9, but without success.

The Kihnu Virve. Source: Kristi Raidla

Ferry company spokesperson: We do not make sufficient profits to meet wage demands

Kihnu Veeteed representative Jaak Kaabel later told ERR that the seafarers' union's expectations are so high that it is quite difficult to meet them. "It must be kept in mind that a month ago the state conciliator, as a neutral party, presented a conciliation proposal, but EMSA rejected that compromise. Instead, it was decided to hold a warning strike today, which makes this conciliation process rather unusual or interesting. The focus is mainly on labor costs," Kaabel said.

"We have boosted wages in recent years, and we have raised them by more than the cost of living has gone up during that time. In that respect, we are in a surprising situation. The other part of the issue is that all our income comes from providing a service to the state through public procurement — namely, operating ferries. There, revenues are fixed, but costs are open-ended. Our profit margin has been around 5 per cent in recent years, so competition in tenders is quite intense. We simply do not have the kind of profits from which we could significantly increase wages," Kaabel went on.

Kihnu Veeteed failed to respond within the deadline to a settlement proposal the national conciliator issued on June 26, the union said, adding the company's positions overall have lacked substance.

Editor's note: This piece was updated to include comment from the Kihnu Veeteed spokesperson.

World.title: Hundreds mark Battle of Tannenberg Line 82nd anniversary in Estonia
World.content:
Close to 400 people turned out to commemorate the 82nd anniversary of the pivotal World War Two Battle of the Tannenberg Line in Ida-Viru County.

This year's attendance was around 100 higher than that seen last year. Organizers say those soldiers who fell fighting for Estonia's freedom deserve greater recognition.

The battles which make up the Battle of the Tannenberg Line, also known as the Battle of the Blue Hills (Estonian: Sinimäed), in July and August 1944 halted the advancing Red Army for several weeks and allowed tens of thousands of Estonians to flee the ensuing occupation, but the state has as yet not formally recognized as freedom fighters or as veterans those who took part, some commentators pointed out.

"They stood for the possibility of restoring the Republic of Estonia. They gave nearly 100,000 people the opportunity to leave Estonia and maintain the government-in-exile. Today's republic does not recognize them. That is a disgrace. The Riigikogu does not have the courage to recognize an Estonian Legion soldier as a freedom fighter and as a veteran," said Martin Sööt, a board member of the Friends of the Estonian Legion club (ELSK).

The legion is controversial in that the Estonian Legion and its successor, expanded units, were organizationally a part of the Waffen SS, a fact which is often seized upon in Russian propaganda.

Attendees at the Tannenberg Line memorial ceremony. Source: ERR

Retired high-ranking army officers and MPs spoke at the anniversary event, pledging to reverse the lack of recognition up to now.

One of the speakers, Maj. Gen. (Retd) Riho Ühtegi, former commander of the Defense League and a potential presidential candidate, rejected the link to Nazism.

"I think the reason for this shame is that people immediately start attaching Nazi symbols to it, but it has absolutely nothing to do with Nazi symbolism. Men fell here whose ideas and mental preparedness were to defend Estonia, not to defend Nazi Germany. Somehow this understanding needs to be changed," Ühtegi told "Aktuaalne kaamera."

MP Arvo Aller (EKRE) said recognizing the veterans of the battles in a manner befitting them should be brought before the relevant Riigikogu committee.

"There is now some commemoration taking place here at this memorial stone, but it should still get somewhat higher recognition. The fighting here was not in vain; it was vital to fight here, and it was vital for the Estonian state," Aller said.

Riho Ühtegi. Source: ERR

Last year's event had been the first time in recent years where politicians had been permitted to speak.

The 1944 defensive battles in the Blue Hills are considered the bloodiest battles in Estonia's history. Nearly 2,500 Estonians alone were killed in the fighting, from July 24 to August 10, 1944.

The memorial was built at the turn of the millennium, to commemorate the Estonians involved.

While the fact that there were Estonians serving in the SS and other World War Two German units is often referred to in Russian propaganda up to the present, a document signed in 1950 by John J. McCloy, chairman of the U.S. investigative committee, found that Baltic units in the Waffen SS were not war criminals and did not follow Nazi ideology.

A much larger Russian force, the Russian Liberation Army, also fought on the German side practically up to the end of the war.

World.title: Skeptics doubt funding for Narva Old Town rebuild
World.content:
Supporters of plans to rebuild part of the historic Old Town in Narva would need to face doubts, including from the city's mayor, over funding for the costly project.

Supporters of the project, which would see replica buildings of the pre-war Old Town built, say it would bring both tourists and investment into the border city.

Model realization of the planned Rüütli tänav quarter reconstruction. Source: ERR

"Private investors are no longer investing in square meterage and concrete. What matters to them is atmosphere, a sense of place and history. And in that respect, Narva has a major competitive advantage," said Vadim Orlov, initiator of the restoration plan, which would focus on Rüütli tänav.

Backed by around 1,000 signatures, the plan is nearing its finalization on paper, though local leaders have expressed doubt about its viability, not the least over funding. No one has yet come forward to actually carry out the work.

Mayor of Narva Katri Raik gave her realistic assessment of the plans coming to fruition any time soon, telling "Aktuaalne kaamera": "It is possible that somewhere in the world there is a – in my opinion, slightly crazy – person who would be willing to invest in Narva's Old Town. But I don't see anyone forthcoming at the moment. I don't see what should be built there or what should be done with whatever gets built there."

Property experts too see no economic rationale in rebuilding the old buildings. Construction can be expensive, particularly in more peripheral areas of the country; there would not be enough customers or business initially to even break even on the project, let alone turn a profit.

Katri Raik. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

The example of the €6 million-plus Town Hall renovation is proof positive of this, the market players say, noting that while there is space for a restaurant to be hosted there, no willing operator has been found in the three years since the reopening.

This pattern repeats elsewhere in the town. "At the moment, there is a great deal of commercial property standing vacant for years. I don't believe that any investor seeking to make a profit would even consider such projects. This would be 100 per cent a charitable undertaking," said property expert Sergei Gorlatsch.

The plans in any case allow for 16 replica buildings, based on the pre-war streetscape in the Rüütli tänav quarter. This area makes up around 10 per cent of Narva's Old Town, which was largely flattened during World War II, particularly during the 1944 Battle of Narva. Once home to a prosperous mercantile community, the quarter, adjacent to the Town Hall Square, is now a green space, enclosed by Soviet-era apartment buildings.

World.title: Bear cubs frolic in Estonian farmyard, right in front of people
World.content:
Three bear cubs were caught on camera strolling around the yard of a Harju County farmhouse last Saturday, seemingly unfazed by the presence of people, Maaleht reported .

Video shared on the Estonian Hunters' Society's Facebook page shows the three cubs playfully exploring the yard of a home in the village of Vanamõisa in Harju County, undeterred by people close by who were loudly trying to ward them off.

Filmed by a member of the Ardu hunting association, the clip shows that the cubs were curious rather than aggressive; the mother bear was nowhere to be seen.

According to zoologist and large carnivore researcher Tiit Maran, bear litters have been getting larger over the years: While a decade ago it was common to see a mother bear with just one or two cubs, this year trail cams nationwide have captured several mothers having to deal with three or even four cubs.

Maran says that although Estonia's bear population is generally peaceable so far as human interaction goes, the observed behavior of both species has been evolving, and the more frequent the encounters get, the greater the likelihood of a bad outcome.

A forecast compiled by hunters indicates that the population can grow by as much as 5-10 percent or more per year, a fact which culling proponents have used to justify continued or even increased culls.

In the most recent culling season, which takes place in the fall, 28 animals from a quota of 71 were hunted. Culls of bears and other animals have sometimes been suspended due to injunctions. One recent high-profile report of a supposed attack by a bear on a human was met with skepticism.

The Environmental Board says brown bears in Estonia usually do not desire to attack humans. If a bear stands up or makes a bluff charge, it is often trying to assess the situation or scare off what it sees as a threat, rather than to attack.

The best way to stay safe is to avoid encounters altogether. Make noise while walking in the forest, watch for signs of bears such as claw marks or tracks, and always keep dogs on a leash, as bears generally prefer to avoid people. If you see a bear cub, back away slowly, as its mother is likely nearby.

World.title: Gallery: 9,000 enjoy second day of Viljandi Folk Music Festival
World.content:
Around 9,000 people attended day two of the Viljandi Folk Music Festival, which runs until today, Sunday.

On Friday, the second day of the event, the most popular concerts featured Latvian folk singer Laima Jansone, Swedish act Groupa, and local talent Eesti ETNO 30, Mari Kalkun, Zetod and Untsakad.

This is the 33rd Viljandi Folk Music Festival, an event which has grown over the years. This time around, about 60 bands and solo artists took part in the traditional opening parade through the south Estonian town.

This year's theme focuses on musical instruments, including a hands-on area where visitors can try traditional folk instruments, and after drawing 38,000 visitors last year, organizers say they expect to break the previous attendance and ticket sales record.

The festival ends at midnight Sunday.

World.title: Border authorities apprehend illegal migrants in Estonia for 4th day in a row
World.content:
The Police and Border Guard Board has stepped up checks at the border and transport hubs to catch illegal border crossers believed to be arriving in Estonia via Latvia.

Over 30 migrants have been detained in Tallinn in recent days, thought to be the result of a surge in illegal immigration at the Latvia-Belarus border.

Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) officers intercepted another group of illegal border crossers at the Old City Harbor A Terminal in Tallinn on Saturday morning. The group had been attempting to travel to Finland, marking the fourth consecutive day migrants have been apprehended in Estonia.

The PPA says it and other authorities are quick to spot migrants, who may for instance appear to be unsure of their surroundings, meaning they seldom get far.

"Quite often, the people who arrive are not regular travelers here. They are looking around, they are not very familiar with the port, and naturally attract the attention of our patrols. We try to speak with them, to see whether they need any assistance, then if it turns out, for example, that they have no legal basis to stay, then that person has to be detained," Tauri Koppel, field commander at the PPA's Tallinn border crossing point, told "Aktuaalne kaamera."

Tallinn's A-Terminal. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

The PPA also inspects vehicles by random spot checks – vehicles whose interiors are not visible from the outside, for instance vans, or passenger vehicles with tinted glass, are often singled out for further scrutiny, though no migrants have been found traveling in this way in recent times.

Many migrants are apparently of African origin and have arrived in Estonia from neighboring Latvia, which in turn borders with Belarus. That country has been directing migrants to its western borders in recent years, which authorities have called "hybrid warfare" and which started in significant numbers in the summer of 2021.

Latvia's National Security Council this week discussed the issue and concluded that the technical border surveillance infrastructure is still not fully complete, and additional measures are also planned.

"There is also a specific package of measures that will be implemented by the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defense. The public will be informed when these measures begin to be introduced, and their results will then become visible. I believe that together we can solve this problem, but it will require considerable effort and a certain departure from the usual approach that has been in place in recent months," Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs said.

Estonia has already sent two units southwards to assist in Latvia, and, at the proposal of the PPA's director general, another two units are to be deployed. Lithuanian and Finnish personnel are also contributing at the Latvian border.

Latvian border guard at the frontier with Belarus. Source: ERR

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) visited the Latvian border this week, to see the situation at first hand. "You can clearly see that they have deployed all available resources there, but the pressure is so great. The people who the Belarusian regime is driving into the forests to attack the Schengen external border can behave quite brazenly. They arrive with long ladders, try to climb over the fence, and when they are shouted at from the other side to go back, they say, 'No, we're coming anyway,'" Taro said, adding "it is certainly not viable to let them in. Otherwise, our entire society will have to deal with this problem. Latvia's deportation and asylum seeker centers are already overcrowded."

Migrants have been apprehended at various locations across Tallinn in recent days, not only in the harbor area but also in the residential outer suburb of Nõmme. The groups were reportedly traveling separately, and at least one public tip-off was received during the PPA operation. While those detained lacked valid documentation, it is believed they originated from various African states and had not been planning to stay in Estonia, instead attempting to reach Finland and then travel onward to Western Europe.

The bulk of those detained have applied for international protection and are being held in a detention center while their claims get processed. Unsuccessful asylum applicants face potential deportation from the country.

While the Belarusian regime has been engaging in hybrid warfare tactics against the EU, particularly Latvia, Lithuania and Poland, which it borders, tighter checks in some neighboring countries and easier travel conditions in summer have led to a rise in illegal migration cases, Estonian border officials say. Just under 150 people were apprehended as illegal migrants in Estonia in the first half of 2026, authorities say.

World.title: Iraq, Lebanon discuss economic partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said on Sunday that it is important to establish economic partnerships with Lebanon in different sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during discussions held in Baghdad with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and his accompanying delegation, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two leaders co-chaired discussions between the two countries, where ministers from both sides attended.

The discussions focused on improving bilateral ties in economic, political, and security areas. They also addressed approaches to strengthen the two countries’ partnership to promote comprehensive and long-term development and benefit both the Iraqi and Lebanese people.

Al-Zaidi also highlighted Iraq and Lebanon’s close friendship, dedication to development, and the need to form beneficial economic collaborations across all development areas.

The prime minister also emphasized the importance of joint coordination between the two nations in addressing regional challenges and supporting efforts to boost stability, reduce tensions, and resolve disputes.

World.title: Washington rejects Iraq’s deal with Turkmenistan to import gas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s plan to purchase Turkmen gas has encountered another obstacle, as the US has raised objections to Baghdad’s proposal to transport the supplies through Iranian territory.

A source told Attaqa News that the United States has connected the agreement’s execution to negotiating a comprehensive political solution with Tehran, complicating the issue of obtaining the fuel required to run Iraq’s power plants.

The US position emerged during talks held in Washington by a government delegation accompanying Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which included Electricity Minister Ali Wahib and Oil Minister Basim Khudair.

The two sides discussed energy and economic cooperation, but the Turkmen gas sale to Iraq via Iran drew strong American opposition, despite Baghdad’s urgent need for new fuel sources amid a worsening electricity crisis.

The rejection comes amid escalating military operations in the Middle East, with the United States and Iran exchanging attacks, as well as rising tensions in the Arabian Gulf, which have affected maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq signed a memorandum of understanding in 2023 with Turkmenistan to import the necessary gas for its power plants, as stated by the Ministry of Electricity. The ministry indicated that the initiative will necessitate additional negotiations regarding the transportation of gas through Iran.

Power plants in Iraq depend on gas imports from Iran, which cover one-third of the country’s energy needs.

This agreement permits Iran to receive a quarter of the gas supplied across its borders.

The gas supply agreement with Turkmenistan aims to provide Iraq with an average of 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraqi court seizes IQD 27 billion in Jumaili’s case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s anti-corruption judiciary has seized IQD 27 billion in cash as part of an ongoing investigation involving Adnan Al-Jumaili, the detained former Deputy Oil Minister for Refining Affairs, in one of the country’s latest high-profile corruption cases.

Judicial authorities said the money was recovered during investigations into alleged financial losses linked to projects overseen by the former official and other individuals connected to the case.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the media office of Iraq’s judiciary said Judge Diaa Jaafar, the investigating judge at the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, confirmed the seizure of IQD 27 billion.

According to the court, the funds were discovered after investigators traced financial proceeds allegedly generated through waste and irregularities in projects associated with Al-Jumaili and other suspects.

Officials said the cash had been hidden by several individuals believed to be involved in the case. The court said investigators are continuing to pursue additional suspects and trace other assets that may be linked to the alleged offenses.

Judicial authorities indicated that the investigation remains active as efforts continue to identify everyone involved and recover additional public funds, if any are found.

The judiciary also released photographs showing stacks of newly recovered banknotes arranged in large piles following the seizure. According to the statement, the images document the IQD 27 billion recovered during Sunday’s operation, which authorities said had been concealed by individuals connected to the former deputy minister.

Officials did not disclose how many people are under investigation or provide further details about the locations where the money was found.

The case is among several recent corruption investigations pursued by Iraq’s anti-corruption courts as authorities seek to recover public funds and hold officials accountable for alleged financial crimes.

The judiciary reiterated that investigations remain ongoing and that further legal action could follow as additional evidence emerges.

World.title: Iraq completes initial designs for Development Road Project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has completed the preliminary designs for its flagship Development Road Project and railway corridor, marking a major milestone as the government prepares to advance one of its largest infrastructure initiatives into the implementation phase.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Sunday that the initial designs are now 100% complete, with work shifting to detailed engineering plans covering infrastructure, bridges, railway stations, and technical facilities along the project’s route.

According to a source at the ministry’s media office, engineers have begun preparing the project’s detailed designs to ensure the corridor meets international engineering and construction standards. The next phase includes finalizing plans for the railway network, highways, bridges, stations, and supporting infrastructure before construction begins.

Officials described the transition as a key step toward launching the long-awaited project after completing the necessary preparatory stages.

The announcement follows a recent visit by Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu to Baghdad on July 21, where he held talks with Iraqi officials on strengthening cooperation in transport and communications.

During the meetings, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahb Al-Hassani and his Turkish counterpart agreed to accelerate technical planning and implementation procedures for the Development Road Project.

The ministry said both sides consider the corridor a transformative initiative that could reshape regional trade and economic cooperation. The ministry also revealed that Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has instructed officials to prepare a comprehensive financing mechanism for the project.

Securing funding will be a priority ahead of the project’s implementation and is expected to feature prominently during Al-Zaidi’s upcoming visit to Ankara, where discussions with Turkish officials will focus on advancing strategic cooperation and moving the project toward construction.

The Development Road Project is designed to create a major transport corridor linking Iraq’s ports with regional and international markets. The combined railway and highway network aims to connect the Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq with Turkey and Europe, positioning Iraq as a key logistics hub between Asia and Europe.

Officials say the corridor will significantly improve trade flows while strengthening Iraq’s role in global supply chains. Alongside the engineering work, the Ministry of Transport is preparing the project’s economic model to maximize investment returns and attract local and international partners.

The ministry said the framework will also align with the government’s broader reform agenda, including digital transformation and modern project management systems.

The government views the Development Road Project as one of Iraq’s most important strategic investments. Officials expect it to diversify the economy beyond oil, generate new non-oil revenues, attract foreign investment, and create thousands of jobs across multiple sectors.

By leveraging Iraq’s geographic position between East and West, the project is also expected to strengthen the country’s role as a regional center for transportation, logistics, and international trade.

World.title: Iraq’s non-oil revenues jump to 16%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Eco Iraq Observatory, which studies economic performance indicators, disclosed on Saturday that non-oil income now accounts for 16 percent of Iraq’s overall financial revenues, the highest percentage recorded so far.

According to a statement released by the observatory, this is the first time that the percentage of non-oil earnings has climbed to 16 percent during the months of May and June, having not exceeded five percent in years.

Eco Iraq noted that the proportion originally grew to roughly 10 percent between May 2020 and October 2022, then remained stable at that level during Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s leadership before recently hitting its peak.

The statement highlighted that non-oil revenues are divided into commodity taxes, production fees, general fees, income and wealth taxes, transfer revenues, and other sources.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s income, which it distributes to the federal government in Baghdad, accounts for around 5.5 percent of overall non-oil revenues.

As part of the government’s efforts to diversify the economy and achieve Iraq’s long-term development goals, Mazhar Saleh, the Prime Minister’s Advisor for Financial Affairs, stated in early June that an initiative would be launched. This initiative aims to create an integrated link between enhancing the structure of non-oil revenues within the framework of state finances and diversifying the non-oil GDP.

The Iraqi government established the ambitious goal, referred to as ‘Iraq 2035,’ in May. It includes both public finance reforms and social market economy policies, which aim to facilitate a gradual structural transformation of the national economy, as stated by Saleh.

The vision transforms fiscal policy to ensure that non-oil income accounts for at least 46 percent of total governmental revenues. This will improve budgetary sustainability and reduce the volatility caused by overreliance on oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq to launch ferry routes to Iran, Kuwait, UAE, and Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is preparing to launch a network of regular maritime passenger routes connecting the country with Iran, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia, as part of a broader effort to revive the country’s maritime transport sector and strengthen regional tourism.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the initiative will begin after technical and administrative requirements are completed in coordination with relevant authorities inside Iraq and neighboring countries.

A source at the ministry’s media office told Iraq’s official newspaper that the government has developed a comprehensive plan to operate regional maritime transport services using an expanded fleet of boats and ferries.

The ministry currently operates 40 boats and ferries under its river transport program and has recently added 15 new boats and three ferries to the fleet. The upgraded vessels are expected to provide modern, safe transportation for passengers while supporting Iraq’s growing tourism sector.

According to the ministry, most of the new vessels will be deployed on passenger and tourism routes linking Iraq with Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Iran. Officials said services will begin once all operational approvals, safety procedures, and cross-border coordination have been finalized to ensure the routes meet international maritime safety standards.

The planned connections are expected to facilitate both tourism and commercial travel between Iraq and neighboring countries. The Ministry of Transport believes the new maritime routes will provide an affordable and practical alternative for regional travel, particularly for leisure tourism.

The project is also expected to improve mobility for official delegations and religious visitors while strengthening economic ties with Gulf states and Iran through enhanced passenger connectivity.

Officials described the initiative as a significant step toward revitalizing Iraq’s maritime transport sector after years of limited regional ferry services. The ferry project forms part of a wider government strategy to modernize Iraq’s river and maritime transport infrastructure.

Alongside expanding its fleet, the ministry is investing in the development of ports, docks, and river terminals to improve passenger services and operational efficiency.

The broader vision aims to restore river and maritime transport as an important component of Iraq’s transportation network while supporting economic development, tourism, and greater regional integration.

World.title: Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate accuses BP of sidelining local talent and demands an 85% local hiring quota
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate has voiced strong concerns over hiring practices and subcontract awards linked to BP’s operations in the province’s oil fields, alleging that local engineers and businesses are being overlooked in favor of workers and companies from outside Kirkuk.

While welcoming international investment in Iraq’s energy sector, the syndicate warned it would pursue legal action and peaceful protests if local employment requirements are not enforced.

In a statement, the syndicate said it is closely monitoring recruitment procedures and the awarding of secondary contracts related to BP’s projects in Kirkuk.

It argued that the current approach has resulted in several violations, including the exclusion of qualified local engineers despite the availability of experienced graduates and professionals from the province.

The syndicate also claimed that engineering and technical staff are being recruited from outside Kirkuk, while numerous subcontracting and logistics contracts have been awarded to companies based elsewhere.

According to the statement, these practices undermine the local economy and deprive Kirkuk residents of employment opportunities linked to projects operating within their province.

The syndicate stressed that Kirkuk residents bear the environmental and health impacts associated with oil production and should therefore receive priority in employment opportunities.

It called on the Ministry of Oil and the Kirkuk provincial administration to require that at least 85% of jobs across all project stages be reserved exclusively for residents of Kirkuk.

In addition, the syndicate demanded formal representation on the joint recruitment committee to ensure transparency and fairness in hiring decisions. It also urged authorities to use the syndicate’s database of registered engineering graduates when filling vacancies.

Among its proposals, the syndicate called for all job applications to be processed exclusively through the employment office of the Kirkuk Governorate, arguing that a centralized system would improve transparency and ensure equal access to opportunities.

The organization also backed government efforts to distribute employment opportunities fairly among all communities in Kirkuk without discrimination.

The statement concluded with a warning that the syndicate would not remain silent if local engineers continue to be excluded from employment opportunities.

It said it is prepared to coordinate with legislative and executive authorities and pursue all available legal avenues, alongside peaceful protests, to protect the rights of Kirkuk’s engineering community. The statement did not include a response from BP regarding the allegations.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank improves non-bank financial oversight
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – As part of a major institutional reform, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) upgraded its Directorate of Non-Bank Financial Institutions Supervision to a complete General Directorate.

This change intends to increase regulatory control, develop digital solutions, and improve institutional performance in Iraq’s expanding financial industry.

The reform entails significant changes to departments, name practices, and reporting structures.

The newly established general directorate will include all important departments in charge of policy, regulatory structures, digital technologies, and financial service operations.

The Information Technology and Payments Directorate is now known simply as the Information Technology Directorate. Its old financial inclusion and information security sections have been removed and merged with risk management and other operational directorates.

The CBI closed its office for coordinating branch activities. The major branches in Basra, Mosul, and Erbil will report directly to the bank’s deputy governor.

The Human Resources Directorate has directed that all personnel transfers and systemic transitions will be effective by July 30, 2026.

This change corresponds with CBI Governor Nizar Hussein’s increasing regulatory push on financial technology businesses to decrease cash dependency and adhere to international compliance requirements.

World.title: 'Attempt to repair PM's tarnished image': Congress on high-powered exam reforms task force
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement of a high-powered task force on examination reforms, the Congress on Sunday termed it a "high-powered attempt" by the prime minister to "repair" his "irreparably tarnished image.

"

"Friends, in June 2024, after irregularities in several exams, including NEET-UG, the Modi government formed a high-level expert committee chaired by former ISRO chairman Dr K. Radhakrishnan to 'ensure the transparent, smooth, and fair conduct of examinations.' In July 2026, after irregularities once again in NEET-UG and other exams, the Modi government has formed a 'high-level task force' to focus on exam reforms," Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X shortly after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement.

He added that the government was yet to fully implement the 101 recommendations made by the Radhakrishnan committee.

"Instead, for nearly two years between 2024 and 2026, it did not even appoint a full-time director general for the National Testing Agency (NTA). Ultimately, all of this is nothing but a high-powered attempt to repair the Prime Minister's irreparably tarnished image," Ramesh said.

PM Modi's announcement came amid demands for examination reforms following the NEET (UG) question paper leak controversy, which affected over 22 lakh aspirants.





On Saturday, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical platform, ended its indefinite sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and broader education reforms.

CJP ended its agitation hours after Pradhan resigned, as student protests intensified in Delhi and other parts of the country. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi has been given additional charge of the Ministry of Education.

Meanwhile, besides Nilekani, who co-founded IT giant Infosys, other members of the high-powered task force include former Isro chairman S Somanath, ex-Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.

According to the prime minister, the government will implement the task force's recommendations to establish a "foolproof examination system."

The panel will help revamp NTA examinations, with a focus on technology-driven improvements and structural reforms in the system, PM Modi added.

World.title: CDSCO cancels 7 clinical trial ethics panels over serious violations
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has cancelled the registration of seven Ethics Committees across India overseeing clinical trials after inspections found serious violations of regulatory norms.

The regulator said the committees failed to comply with the New Drugs and Clinical Trials (NDCT) Rules, 2019, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and other requirements, compromising their ability to carry out their responsibilities.

The action covers Ethics Committees in Delhi, Pune, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata, which review and monitor clinical trials to protect the rights, safety and well-being of participants.

The CDSCO said the committees were inspected as part of a risk-based compliance exercise to assess adherence to the NDCT Rules, 2019, Good Clinical Practice guidelines and quality management systems. The inspections identified significant deficiencies and major regulatory non-compliances in the functioning of the committees.

According to the regulator, the registrations were cancelled only after completion of the regulatory process, including evaluation of inspection reports, review of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) responses, issuance of show-cause notices and personal hearings, wherever applicable.





The seven committees whose registrations have been cancelled are Rational Independent Ethics Committee, New Delhi; Hurip Independent Bioethics Committee and Dr T K Pal Memorial Bio Ethics Committee, Kolkata; Ethiwell Ethics Committee and Ethos Ethics Committee, Navi Mumbai; Institutional Ethics Committee, Aatman Hospital, Ahmedabad; and Royal Pune Independent Ethics Committee, Pune.

World.title: ‘Responsible for brutal assault on innocent students’: After Dharmendra Pradhan, opposition turns heat on Amit Shah, seeks resignation
World.content:
File photo: Union home minister Amit Shah

Opposition prepares to corner government in Parliament

Questions over higher education secretary appointment

NEW DELHI: The opposition is set to intensify its attack on the government in Parliament on Monday by demanding the resignation of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas said.Speaking to reporters in New Delhi on Sunday, Brittas said opposition parties would also raise the appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary, department of higher education, when Parliament resumes.The remarks come a day after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following a 36-day agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), with the government also accepting the protesters' other key demands."Last day, Shah said the government respected the youth who led the protest. Where was that respect for the last 36 days? When students were being beaten on the streets of the national capital, and their skulls were being cracked open, where was that respect?" Brittas said."If there is even a grain of sincerity in those words, Amit Shah too should resign. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. The home minister, who is responsible for this brutal assault on innocent students, must resign," he added.Brittas said the opposition would support any move to strengthen laws against examination-related fraud but questioned the government's decision to amend the existing legislation instead of ensuring its implementation.He noted that Parliament had enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2024 after the government claimed it would curb paper leaks."Now the government is only proposing amendments to that law. The problem is not the absence of legislation but the lack of political will to enforce it and the authorities' alleged compromise with vested interests," he claimed.INDIA bloc parties are planning to seek an urgent discussion in Parliament on the alleged use of excessive force against students protesting the NEET paper leak.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has written to home minister Amit Shah seeking accountability, while Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose has submitted a notice in the Rajya Sabha seeking suspension of business to discuss the issue.The opposition is expected to raise allegations regarding the use of pellet guns, the deployment of men in plain clothes during the July 20 protest, and injuries suffered by students. The government, meanwhile, is scheduled to introduce amendments to the anti-paper leak law in the Lok Sabha on Monday.The proposed Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, seeks stricter penalties for paper leaks, including imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 50 lakh for individuals involved, while organised crimes related to examination fraud could attract fines of up to Rs 10 crore.Brittas also questioned the appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary, department of higher education, alleging that the officer had previously faced accusations of irregularities in the disbursal of central government subsidies."Such an officer has now been appointed to head the department responsible for public examinations, where transparency and integrity are of utmost importance. All these issues will be raised during the discussion in Parliament," he said.He further alleged that while authorities had released details of police personnel injured during the protests, no information had been made public about injured students."The home ministry has released details of police personnel who were allegedly injured. But not a single detail has been made public about the protesters who were brutally assaulted. There is a complete veil of secrecy over their condition," Brittas claimed.He said the identities and medical condition of injured students should be disclosed so that their families and organisations willing to assist them could provide support.Separately, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also blamed Amit Shah for the police action during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march organised by the CJP at Jantar Mantar.Raut alleged that students were attacked and women protesters were harassed, holding the home minister responsible for the incident. He also claimed Shah was responsible for "whatever bad and undemocratic is happening in the country."The BJP rejected Raut's remarks, with Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban asking the Shiv Sena (UBT) leader to focus on his "already depleted party".The protests, which began on June 20 over the NEET paper leak, were called off on Saturday after the government accepted key demands of the protesters and Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down as education minister.The July 20 police action against protesters marching towards Parliament has since become a major flashpoint, with opposition parties alleging excessive use of force, including pellet guns.Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns during the protest, while the CRPF has not publicly responded to allegations involving its Rapid Action Force.

World.title: Infosys co-founder, Aadhaar architect: Who is Nandan Nilekani, set to lead high-powered exam reforms task force
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Continuing his announcements on examination reforms, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said the government has constituted a high-powered task force to be led by Infosys co-founder

.

Also Read:

"HIGH-POWERED TASK FORCE on examination reforms under the leadership of Shri Nandan Nilekani constituted," PM Modi said in a video message on X, a day after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical platform, called off its 37-day-long agitation following the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET (UG) question paper leak.

Led by CJP, thousands of students had been on an indefinite sit-in in Delhi since June 21, demanding the resignation or removal of Pradhan and broader reforms in the education sector.

Meanwhile, joining Nilekani on the task force are former Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau (IB) director Tapan Deka, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.

Also Read:

Who is Nandan Nilekani

Nilekani is the co-founder and chairman of Bengaluru-headquartered IT giant Infosys. He also served as the founding chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the body that issues Aadhaar cards, with the rank of a Cabinet minister in the Congress-led central government from 2009 to 2014.





In January 2023, he was appointed as the co-chair of the âG20 Task Force on Digital Public Infrastructure for Economic Transformation, Financial Inclusion, and Development.â

Born in Bengaluru, Nilekani, 71, graduated from IIT Bombay in 1978. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian honour, in 2006. Time magazine named him among the world's 100 most influential people in 2006 and 2009, and included him in its 2024 list of the 100 Most Influential People in AI.

Nilekani has also authored or co-authored three books.

World.title: Ex-Isro chief, IIT director & more: Who is on Nandan Nilekani-led NTA exam reforms panel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has constituted a high-powered task force to recommend comprehensive reforms for examinations conducted by the

(NTA), with a focus on strengthening technology, improving logistics and introducing structural changes to the examination system.

The multidisciplinary panel will be headed by technology expert

and comprises experts from education, science, security and administration. Other members include former ISRO chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.

The task force has been mandated to examine ways to make NTA examinations more transparent, secure and technology-driven.

It will recommend reforms to improve the overall examination process, strengthen cybersecurity, enhance logistical planning and restore public confidence in competitive examinations.

The panel was announced as part of the Centre's broader efforts to overhaul the examination system following controversies over alleged paper leaks and examination irregularities. Its recommendations are expected to form the basis for future reforms in the conduct of national-level entrance examinations.

World.title: PM Modi returns with message to students, announces Nandan Nilekani-led task force on exam reforms
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday announced the constitution of a high-powered task force headed by technology expert

to recommend reforms aimed at making India's examination system more reliable, transparent and technology-driven.

In a video message addressed to students, the

said the government had already taken several steps to safeguard the future of students, including action against those involved in examination malpractice, the establishment of fast-track courts and the introduction of tougher legal provisions through new legislation.

"The Government of India is continuously taking various measures for the future of students.

Those who tampered with the students' future are languishing in jail. We have already established fast-track courts. We are also moving towards enacting new legislation in Parliament that incorporates stringent legal provisions. However, we must look to the future. Our examination system needs to be reliable and transparent, and it must make maximum use of technology.

Keeping all these factors in mind, we have decided to constitute a high-powered task force under the leadership of the world-renowned technology expert Nandan Nilekani.





This task force will focus on examination reforms, and based on its report, steps will be taken to ensure the credibility of upcoming examinations at the earliest," PM Modi said.

The announcement comes amid the Centre's push to strengthen the examination process following recent controversies over irregularities in competitive examinations. The government has also proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, providing for time-bound investigations, fast-track trials and enhanced penalties for paper leaks and organised examination fraud.

The Nandan Nilekani-led task force is expected to examine the use of technology and recommend systemic reforms to improve transparency, credibility and efficiency in the conduct of public examinations across the country.

World.title: 'Govt-ordered probe an eyewash': Tripura Congress MLA demands judicial inquiry into DGP Anurag Dhankar's death
World.content:
Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar was found dead in state police headquarters on July 20

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman on Sunday reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe into the death of state DGP Anurag Dhankar, who was found dead at the police headquarters in Agartala on July 20."From day one, we have been demanding a judicial probe by a sitting high court judge into the unnatural death of the DGP, keeping in mind the circumstances leading to the recovery of his body," he told a press conference at the Congress Bhavan in Agartala."The condition in which we saw his body at the morgue was as if he was in deep sleep, with no visible wounds that are generally found in such cases. We strongly believe that a team led by an SP-rank officer cannot clear the many doubts surrounding the incident.That is why we want a judicial inquiry into the unnatural death," Roy Barman added.A three-member team headed by West Tripura SP Namit Pathak has been constituted to investigate the matter.Roy Barman termed the Tripura government's decision to investigate the case through a three-member team as an "eyewash." He alleged that the "honest DGP was heckled over some issues days before his death."The Congress MLA also expressed disappointment over the Tripura high court not taking suo motu cognisance of Dhankar's death."The people of the state are also upset over the role of our high court. When the legislature, bureaucracy and media succumb, it is the judiciary that comes out and stands for the cause of people's rights. Unfortunately, we have not seen the high court take any suo motu cognisance in many incidents in the state since former Chief Justice Deepak Kumar Gupta's tenure ended," he said.Dhankar, a native of Uttar Pradesh's Baghpat, was a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Tripura cadre. He took over as the state's DGP in May 2025.The officer had led the CBI probe into the alleged Rs 13,000-crore Punjab National Bank fraud involving diamantaire Nirav Modi and the reinvestigation into the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

World.title: From Chita Andolan to Jal Satyagrahas: Why the Ken-Betwa project has upset MP tribals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: They first stood in the river. Then they lay beside funeral pyres. When that, too, failed to draw a response, they climbed symbolic gallows.

Over the past month, the 'Chita Andolan' in Madhya Pradesh has transformed an otherwise local land acquisition dispute into one of the country's most striking protest movements, that was forcefully ended by the administration, citing threats to protesters due to rising water levels.

Its haunting imagery, however, has thrown a spotlight on the repercussions that the Ken-Betwa River Linking Project, a flagship infrastructure initiative that promises water security for millions but has also triggered a fierce battle over compensation, will have on the locals, questioning the rehabilitation and the rights of tribal communities facing displacement.

The movement gathered further attention after activist Amit Bhatnagar completed an 18-day hunger strike, insisting he had only suspendedânot endedâhis fast because "until the last person gets justice, the fast will continue."

Bhatnagar broke the hunger strike because villagers, especially women and children and 400 leading social activists from across the country, including

appealed to him since his health had started deteriorating. But it was the government's assurance of a fresh survey to include the names of those left out from rehabilitation that changed his decision.

Bhatnagar's protest became the face of growing resistance to the 'Ken-Betwa River Linking Project', India's first river-linking initiative under the National Perspective Plan.





The Centre and the Madhya Pradesh government hail the project as a landmark intervention that will transform the drought-prone Bundelkhand region through irrigation, drinking water supply and power generation. But for thousands of tribal families living in its path, it has become a battle over land, forests, livelihoods and identity.

Over the past month, villagers have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations.

They stood waist-deep in river water in 'Jal Satyagraha', lay beside symbolic funeral pyres in the 'Chita Andolan' and even climbed symbolic gallows in a 'Faansi Satyagraha'.

Police eventually cleared the protest site on July 19, citing safety concerns due to rising water levels in the Barana river. Protesters alleged they were forcibly removed, while the administration maintained that the evacuation was necessary to prevent loss of life.

The movement has revived questions India has wrestled with since the Narmada Bachao Andolan: Can large infrastructure projects be built without sacrificing the rights of the communities that bear their greatest costs?

TIMELINE | Ken-Betwa Project

A project decades in the making



The Ken-Betwa Link Project has its origins in the National Perspective Plan for interlinking rivers proposed in 1980. After decades of planning, agreements and environmental clearances, the Union Cabinet approved the project in 2021, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid its foundation stone in December 2024.

The project proposed to transfer what the government describes as surplus water from the Ken river to the Betwa river through the Daudhan Dam, tunnels and a 221-kilometre canal.

The project is expected to irrigate 10.61 lakh hectares, providing drinking water to around 65 lakh people in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, generating 103 MW of hydropower and 27 MW of solar power and reduce the chronic water scarcity that has plagued Bundelkhand for decades.

Officials argue that it will boost agricultural productivity, reduce migration and improve groundwater recharge by restoring historical Chandela-era ponds.

For supporters, however, it is a long-awaited solution to one of central India's most persistent development challenges.

The surplus water of Ken River will be transferred to Betwa River through the 221 km long link canal from Daudhan Dam, providing irrigation and drinking water facilities in both MP and UP.

Why are people protesting?

For many tribal families in Chhatarpur and Panna districts, the project threatens the loss of ancestral land without adequate rehabilitation.

Bhatnagar says the issue extends far beyond compensation. "Our demand is that people should be given land in exchange for land. But even if the government only fulfils what it has committed, that much should at least be delivered."

He argues that tribal communities who depend on forests cannot rebuild their lives simply through financial assistance. "People who are being displaced from forests should either be resettled in forest areas or, at the very least, they should be given land and a village to live in.

That has been our main demand from the beginning."

The state government had announced an in-principle increase in the rehabilitation package from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 12.5 lakh per eligible displaced family, with a formal notification expected.

Bhatnagar, however, says the revised compensation alone does not solve the problem. "The way these people lived in forests and depended on the forest, simply giving them Rs 12.5 lakh is not enough."

He claims many displaced villagers have little experience navigating land markets and are vulnerable to exploitation. "Unscrupulous people are misleading them by offering fake land at cheap prices. They end up buying fake land or fake houses. Later they discover that the property itself was fraudulent. They lose both their money and then get trapped in legal disputes."

TIMELINE | CHITA ANDOLAN

One of the biggest disagreements concerns the number of affected families.

The government estimates that around 7,100 families are affected by the Ken-Betwa project. Bhatnagar disputes that figure.

"In the Ken-Betwa project, the government says there are 7,100 affected families. But the actual number is around 10,000, in fact more than 10,000. If we talk about all the projects together, nearly 50,000 people have been affected."

He alleges that survey teams have excluded genuine beneficiaries.

"The survey teams have included the names of many fake beneficiaries. For example, in one village where Rs 11 crore was sanctioned for housing compensation, Rs 8 crore went to fake beneficiaries, while only Rs 3 crore reached the actual villagers."

While the administration has rejected allegations of corruption, a fresh survey team was announced to identify families who may have been left out.

TOI reached out to Chhatarpur district magistrate and is still awaiting a response from the administration.

We will update the story accordingly.

The govt's fresh assurances made Bhatnagar suspend his hunger strike. "The administration did whatever it could from its side. It formed a new survey team for those people who had been left out. Our farmers' organisation has also been included in that survey team so that the names of everyone who was left out can be properly verified."

"We remain hopeful. But the officers and employees working for the government function very slowly.

Their pens don't move unless money is involved. We have faith in the government. But if the government does not do this, then our protest will continue," he warned, despite being hopeful.

The unique protest has drawn national attention.

How the 'Chita Andolan' was born

Perhaps the most striking aspect of the movement has been its symbolism.

The image of tribal families lying beside funeral pyres captured national attention and prompted comparisons with the Narmada Bachao Andolan's iconic Jal Satyagrahas.

Bhatnagar says the idea emerged after protesters felt every avenue of democratic dissent had been blocked. "Wherever we tried to protest, Section 144 notices were imposed. People were intimidated. When we were trying to go to Delhi, we were stopped, our vehicles fined, our entire stock of rations looted. We were stopped at several places."

He alleges that even after the movement got restricted to the villages, essential supplies were cut off.

"Food and water were cut off. Water tankers were removed. Even the borewell that was supplying water was shut down. We were forced to drink river water."

Then came the thought that gave the protest its name.

"If they are trying to kill us anyway, if our own government wants us to die, then let us light our own funeral pyre," said Bhatnagar.

As restrictions tightened, the forms of protest evolved.

"There were other forms of protest too, like standing in the river.

Then the Jal Satyagraha began. After that, they stopped our ration, food, medicines and even doctors from reaching us. Then they threatened us, saying they would hang us. So we ourselves climbed onto the gallows. That is how one form of protest after another kept evolving."

Why was the protest site cleared

The protest took another turn on July 19, when police dispersed demonstrators. Officials said continuous rainfall had raised the river level, making the site unsafe, and shifted Bhatnagar to hospital after his health deteriorated.

Bhatnagar alleges that women were injured during the operation. "Women's sarees were torn, many women lost their mangalsutras, and many people were injured. Naturally, there is a lot of anger among the people," he said.

Despite the anger, he insists the movement remains committed to non-violence.

"We follow Gandhian principles and believe in democratic values. We do not want such things. Yes, there is tremendous anger.

There is pain. Our effort is to maintain a balance between that pain and anger, and to ensure that people get justice through the right path," he said.

More than one project

While public attention has focused on the Ken-Betwa link, Bhatnagar says the movement also represents people affected by the Majhgaon and Runjh irrigation projects.

"There are five such projects in Chhatarpur and Panna where the law has not been followed."

He says surveys have restarted only in a limited area. "Right now, this process has begun only in a small area, in 11 villages of the Chhatarpur project.

The people of Panna district have not yet received any response."

The larger debate



The Ken-Betwa project has also faced criticism from environmental groups concerned about the impact of the Daudhan Dam on parts of the Panna Tiger Reserve. Conservationists have questioned forest submergence and biodiversity loss, while the government says all necessary environmental clearances have been obtained and mitigation measures are in place.

Ultimately, the dispute has become larger than one dam or one canal.

It reflects a recurring question in India's development journey: Can projects that promise benefits for millions be implemented without leaving displaced communities behind?

For the government, the Ken-Betwa project is a blueprint for India's future water security.

For many tribal families living along the Barana river, it is a fight to ensure that development does not come at the cost of their homes, livelihoods and identity.

As survey teams begin their work once again, the project's success may ultimately depend not only on engineering but on whether the promises of rehabilitation and justice reach every family that stands to lose the most.

World.title: Iran says progress in Oman talks on Hormuz Strait management
World.content:
Iran said on Sunday (July 26, 2026) it had made progress in talks with Oman on management of the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway crucial for oil and gas trade that both countries border.

The latest talks come after the United States resumed attacks on Iran in an effort to end Tehran's control of the Strait, following a June memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the war that had briefly eased tensions.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said several rounds of negotiations were held in the Iranian capital, Tehran, on Friday (July 24) and Saturday (July 25) between Iranian and Omani deputy Foreign Ministers.

The discussions focused on "common principles and operational mechanisms" for ensuring the safe passage of shipping through the strait while respecting the sovereign rights of the two states, Mr. Baqaei said.

He described the talks as "useful" and said progress had been made, adding that "technical and political consultations between the two sides were continuing".

Also Read | What is Greater Tunb Island, the strategic point in the Strait of Hormuz targeted by U.S. airstrikes?

In June, Oman and Iran said they would discuss imposing service fees, a move Washington opposes.

But Muscat also said ships could transit Hormuz via its waters, angering Tehran, which responded with a pattern of escalation. Iran said on Saturday that it had not recorded any US attacks after nearly two weeks of strikes.

According to news site Axios, the Pentagon presented US President Donald Trump with a plan for a 14th consecutive night of strikes, but he declined to authorise it in favour of renewed talks.

The report said Trump made the order to hold fire after an Omani delegation arrived in Tehran "for talks on a new arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz".

Responding to a separate question, Mr. Baqaei said there had been "no change" in the status of shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

On Sunday, Iran's armed forces stopped six vessels attempting to transit the Hormuz Strait after warnings over the past 24 hours, according to state television.

World.title: Two brothers found dead in a well in Theni district
World.content:
Two brothers, aged 10 and 11, were found dead with external injuries in a well inside a private farm at Bodinayakkanur in Theni district on Saturday.

Following a complaint, the police registered a case. Superintendent of Police K.S. Praveen Gautham, Deputy Superintendent of Police Murugan and other officials inspected the scene.

The police said Chinnathambi, son of Subbiah, was living with his family on Ambedkar Street. His two sons had failed to return home from school on Friday, following which the family lodged a complaint. The police registered a missing case and launched a search.

Under such circumstances, the bodies of the two children were later found in a well inside a coconut farm. The police recovered the bodies and sent them to the Government Hospital for post-mortem.

A senior officer said that though the exact motive was yet to be established, they were examining a few leads. When the post-mortem report was released, we might get some definite clues, he added.

The brothers were studying in a government-aided school. Their father was a daily-wage worker in the locality.

World.title: Bandi challenges Revanth to back Gen Z push with Cabinet berths
World.content:
Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, on Sunday, hit back at Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy over his proposal to reduce the minimum age for contesting Assembly and Lok Sabha elections from 25 to 21 years, challenging him to first induct Gen Z leaders into the State Cabinet.

Addressing the media at Shamshabad Airport, Mr. Sanjay said that if the Chief Minister was serious about empowering the younger generation, he should allot ministerial berths to leaders in the 21-30 age group instead of merely advocating constitutional amendments.

The BJP leader also demanded that the State government ask sitting Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) to resign and nominate Gen Z leaders in their place if it genuinely wanted to provide greater political representation to young people.

Claiming that the Home, Education and Municipal Administration portfolios were yet to be filled, Mr. Sanjay Kumar urged the Chief Minister to entrust these departments to young leaders.

In a swipe at the Congress, he questioned whether senior leaders were being projected as representatives of Gen Z. He alleged that the Congress had a history of appointing elderly leaders to posts meant for the youth.

World.title: Govt firm on 50% merit quota for Pharm D admissions: Minister
World.content:
Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said that the State government remains firm on its stance that it will not compromise on its decision to reserve 50% of seats for merit-based admissions to Pharm D (Doctor of Pharmacy) course from this academic year. Challenging the government’s decision, the Kerala State Self Financing Pharmacy College Management Association has approached the High Court, seeking permission to continue admissions to all Pharm D seats independently.

In a statement, the office of the Health Minister stated that the government’s decision to introduce a 50% merit quota is aimed at ensuring that deserving students are not denied admission solely because they cannot afford the higher fees associated with management admissions.

Mr. Muraleedharan recently held discussions with representatives of the association, during which the managements reiterated their main demand. Nonetheless, the Minister indicated that the government could consider another demand raised by the association to transfer any merit seats remaining vacant after the admission process to the management quota.

World.title: Flavio Bolsonaro gets party nod to take on Lula in Brazil polls
World.content:
Brazil's right-wing Liberal Party on Saturday (July 26, 2026) formally nominated Flavio Bolsonaro, a 45-year-old senator and son of imprisoned ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, as its candidate in the October Presidential election.

He is set to face off against leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 80, who is seeking a fourth nonconsecutive term and has gained momentum in recent weeks as the younger Bolsonaro faced a series of crises.

Far-right firebrand Jair Bolsonaro anointed his eldest son Flavio as his political heir after being sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup following his 2022 election loss to Lula.

"I may be calmer, more cheerful, more composed and more moderate, but Bolsonaro blood flows here!" Mr. Flavio, touching his arm, declared to a cheering crowd in a Sao Paulo warehouse.

He warned that Brazil —Latin America's largest country in population, area and economy — "could take giant strides toward a dictatorship" if Mr. Lula wins reelection.

That alarmist rhetoric was echoed by Argentina's libertarian President Javier Milei, who joined the convention in person to lend support to Flavio Bolsonaro.

"I firmly believe there is no one else capable of putting an end to the Lula risk hanging over Brazil," Mr. Milei said in a typically fiery speech.

Wearing Brazilian national team jerseys, which have become a symbol of the Bolsonaro movement, supporters beat drums and waved flags inside a warehouse next to Sao Paulo's Pacaembu Stadium.

"We would have liked our candidate to be Jair Bolsonaro, but today Flavio is the best choice," Fernando Moeno, a 50-year-old retired military police officer attending the convention, told AFP.

Flavio Bolsonaro teared up as he referenced his father, who appeared in an AI-generated video. Courts have barred the ex-president from making political statements while he serves his sentence under house arrest.

Promising to crack down on crime and inflation, Mr. Flavio was neck-and-neck with Mr. Lula in the polls until he was hit by a series of scandals: ties to a disgraced banker, a family feud, and new tariffs imposed by ally U.S. President Donald Trump.

Pollster Datafolha published a survey Friday showing that in a runoff election, Mr. Lula would win 48% of the votes to Mr. Flavio's 43%.

A wave of scandals

Mr. Flavio's troubles began in May when an audio recording leaked of him asking banker Daniel Vorcaro — accused in a multi-million-dollar fraud case — to finance a film about his father.

Mr. Flavio initially denied any contact with Mr. Vorcaro and told a reporter that the accusation was "a lie." He now says their relationship was limited to the movie.

On Thursday, a Supreme Court justice ordered an investigation into the financing of the film.

Then Mr. Flavio's stepmother, Michelle Bolsonaro, posted an Instagram video saying he had "disrespected me and mistreated me...he said I didn't understand anything about politics."

The former first lady is key to the right-wing movement's appeal among Brazil's large female and evangelical electorate.

Mr. Flavio then read out a letter on social media from Jair Bolsonaro urging unity — contravening the terms of his father's house arrest, prompting a supreme court justice to deny him visits with Jair until after the first round of voting.

This week, Mr. Flavio posted a video apologizing to Michelle, who quickly accepted the olive branch.

Tariff troubles

Mr. Flavio has cast himself as a more moderate version of his father, but is a hardliner on crime and this week echoed the older Bolsonaro in raising debunked concerns about Brazil's electronic voting system.

A Brazilian diplomatic source said Saturday (July 25) that visas had been denied to U.S. officials seeking talks on election matters over concerns of a "risk of political exploitation."

But a U.S. State Department spokesperson said: "Any insinuation of a 'ploy' to undermine a democratic nation's election is a baseless lie."

The senator has struggled to seal alliances with Brazil's influential centrist bloc, with key parties announcing they will remain neutral in the October 4 election.

Flavio Bolsonaro has also faced backlash after Trump's administration imposed two new rounds of tariffs on Brazil this month.

The Bolsonaro family had backed earlier tariffs imposed in retaliation for the trial of the former president, prompting Lula to accuse them of treason.

World.title: Server issues, shortage of meter readers delay Gruha Jyothi verification
World.content:
With rampant server issues and a fewer number of meter readers on job, the Gruha Jyothi door-to-door verification has slowed down. Launched on July 1, 2026, the Energy Department has been able to verify only around 45 lakh beneficiaries, of the estimated 1.65 crore beneficiaries.

It is unlikely that the department will achieve the herculean target within the set deadline of August 31, with only 21,602 meter readers across the State.

According to the Energy Department officials, Bescom meter readers have completed verification of 25 lakh houses in its jurisdiction with only 7,409 meter readers. There are a total of 65 lakh beneficiaries in the Bescom jurisdiction, and 40 lakh households are yet to be verified.

Server issues

A resident in Malleshpalya in C.V. Raman Nagar said, “Meter readers came around 12 p.m. to our residence for the Gruha Jyothi verification process. It wasn’t even half a day that the server slowed down and the app crashed. After waiting for 20 minutes for the server to recover, meter readers had to leave saying they will visit again.” Another resident in Chandra Layout said, “There are four houses in our building. While my house verification was completed, the meter readers couldn’t complete three more houses of verification due to server being slow.”

When asked about the server issues crippling the survey, a senior Energy Department official explained, “At the end of the process, all the data of Gruha Jyothi is uploaded to the Seva Sindhu portal. Since, multiple utility services, including issuing of Khata under Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), Health Department services, ration card, guarantee schemes including Gruha Lakshmi, Shakti are also captured on this portal and used by multiple users, the server slows down.”

“The meter readers have been working on Saturdays and Sundays also to cover the target of beneficiaries assigned to them. They are visiting a house multiple times, even after working hours to enter details of a particular household if needed,” the official said.

Decided to give up

A senior Energy Department official said that more than 20,000 people who had opted and are benefitting from the Gruha Jyothi guarantee scheme have denied to give any details to the meter readers. “The beneficiaries have opted to give up and signed on Part B in their respective forms. The Part B clearly states that the beneficiary has no objection for discontinuation of the benefit to the electricity connection provided to their home,” the official said.

World.title: BHUTA makes fourth representation in three years for faculty representation in Syndicate under Associate Professor and Professor categories
World.content:
Bharathiar University Teachers’ Association (BHUTA) has made its fourth representation over the past three years to the varsity administration seeking the filling of vacant Syndicate member positions under ‘Associate Professor’ and ‘Professor’ categories.

After the vacancies arose in 2023, the association had made two representations in the subsequent years, and two so far this year for filling the vacancies.

The Syndicate currently has three members from among academic experts nominated by the Chancellor, one university assistant professor nominated by rotation according to seniority, and five college secretaries nominated by the government.

There are apprehensions among the faculty that matters of academic importance do not get due importance in the agendas. For instance, the university is yet to address the long-pending issue of CAS (Career Advancement Scheme) interview for promotions to all eligible faculty members, BHUTA said.

The association has been asking for the implementation of the High Court verdict on inclusion of past service for CAS, withdrawal of audit objections, and due consideration of post-doctoral and prior teaching experience for promotions under CAS.

According to senior professors in the university, representation in the Syndicate under Associate Professor and Professor categories will pave way for their inclusion in the Sub-Committees. Earlier this year, BU had to reconstitute 16 Syndicate Sub-Committees entrusted with key administrative tasks with the available strength of nine members.

The presence of the eight ex-officio members notwithstanding, progress on academic issues specific to the university could be discussed meaningfully only with the representation of Associate Professor and Professor in the Syndicate, BHUTA functionaries emphasise.

The university is required to nominate one associate professor to be nominated by the Vice-Chancellor by rotation according to the seniority. It should also fill three vacancies at the rate of one university professor for every 10 heads of departments of study and research, schools of excellence or centres of advanced studies, or part thereof, to be nominated by rotation from among such departments, schools and centres by the Chancellor on the recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor.

The Higher Education Department’s directive is awaited also for filling two vacancies in the Syndicate for principals of affiliated colleges elected from among themselves; two members elected by teachers of affiliated colleges (other than principals) from among themselves who are members of the Senate; and one member, not falling under any of the above three categories, elected by Senate from among its members.

World.title: Inter-district vehicle-lifting gang busted; 10 arrested
World.content:
Neradigonda police in Adilabad district busted an inter-district vehicle-lifting gang by arresting 10 members and recovering seven motorcycles, three autorickshaws and a car worth around ₹17 lakh.

The arrested persons, all from Nirmal, included alleged kingpins Yasar Ahmed, 25, and Sohail, 25, police said.
